title: Edge Crush Test vs Box Compression Test
html:
An edge crush result describes corrugated board; a box compression result describes an assembled container under its stated test. Check the object, loading direction and unit before comparing supplier numbers. Neither a board figure nor an empty-box result alone establishes a safe payload or stack height for filled shipping cartons.

This guide explains the evidence distinction. No supplier values, laboratory results or actual carton performance have been examined.

Identify the object and the reported quantity

The FEFCO testing directory separates board Method 8 from packaging Method 50. Its public English booklet gives these different scopes:

Evidence What is compressed Reported quantity under the cited method
Method 8 edgewise crush resistance A board specimen loaded along the flutes Maximum force normalized by specimen edge length, in kN/m
Method 50 compression resistance An empty corrugated container, with or without interior fittings, in the agreed direction Maximum container force, in N

The booklet’s Method 8 dates from 1982 with amendments through 1997. Method 50 is dated November 1994, amended March 1997, and includes a later precision study. They are historical public procedures, not a guarantee of the latest 2026 technical revision. Their scope does not authorize an improvised buyer test or a universal acceptance limit.

The current public scope of ISO 3037:2022 specifies a non-waxed edge method with force along the flute axis. A report called ECT still needs its actual method identified; the name alone does not settle whether two results are comparable. The full paid ISO standard was not acquired.

A force-per-length figure cannot be ranked beside whole-box force

Kilonewtons per metre and newtons express different quantities. Converting kN/m to N/m changes the unit scale but still leaves a force-per-length quantity. It does not turn that board result into a measured container force.

Imagine a hypothetical jewelry brand comparing two outer-carton proposals. One supplier returns board ECT information. Another returns a compression result for an erected empty carton with dividers. The buyer has not received two answers to the same question.

If the immediate decision is between board alternatives, request comparable board-property evidence. If it is between carton constructions, ask what evidence addresses each proposed assembled container. Keep the first board figure useful for its material question without treating the second supplier’s different evidence as a directly comparable score.

Two cartons using the same declared board ECT can still differ in dimensions, construction and fittings. Those differences must remain visible when the buyer asks about the container. ECT can be an engineering input; it is not a one-number prediction of every carton configuration.

Separate an empty container from the loaded stacking question

Suppose a candle brand receives an empty-carton compression result but wants to plan storage of cartons holding candle gift boxes. The received report and the desired decision concern different states.

Describe the actual packed arrangement to the technical reviewer: contents, holders, closures, orientation and intended load arrangement. Do not fill those gaps by assigning an invented safety factor or dividing a peak-force figure into a stack count.

The public scope of ISO 12048:1994 addresses complete, filled transport packages and distinguishes compression from stacking tests using a compression tester. ISO lists it as reviewed and confirmed in 2022. The abstract is not the full procedure or a project-specific acceptance rule.

A peak compression result is therefore not automatically evidence for a load maintained under the intended stacking conditions. The responsible reviewer must identify which evaluation or supported engineering assessment answers that question. This article supplies neither a test setup nor permission to stack an actual shipment.

Ask for the evidence that answers the purchasing decision

For the hypothetical jewelry comparison, ask each supplier whether its document concerns board, an empty container or the complete filled package. Then identify the decision still unanswered. A board-only reply leaves container-level evidence open; an empty-box reply leaves the proposed loaded stacking question open.

Before comparing like objects, check their actual method, preparation, loading direction, conditioning and result definition. An upright specimen illustration does not prove that a report used the required flute direction, and a carton photograph does not establish its tested orientation or fittings.

The existing conditioning guide and report-configuration guide help retain those details. The distribution-test scope guide addresses the wider packed system. Use them after identifying the quantity the supplier actually measured.

Sources accessed 9 October 2026. FEFCO’s directory is undated; its linked methods retain their stated historical dates. ISO edition and scope information was read publicly without obtaining the complete paid methods. Packrivo coordinates sourcing and supplier questions; appropriate technical parties own testing, interpretation and acceptance. Any accompanying diagram is an AI-assisted schematic, not a measured result or standards-certified apparatus.

Normalize a unit without turning board evidence into box evidence

Two invented replies name different objects: E-H gives a board value of 6 kN/m, while C-H gives an empty-container value of 2,500 N. Neither report exists. These teaching values are not results for packaging offered by Packrivo.

Invented reply Object and quantity Permitted arithmetic Unanswered question
E-H: 6 kN/m Board; force per edge length 6 kN/m = 6,000 N/m Complete-carton evidence
C-H: 2,500 N Empty container; whole force No conversion to board value Actual filled-system stacking
Filled system requested Contents and conditions to identify No stack count Appropriate evaluation and criteria

Multiplying the board value by 1,000 changes its unit scale, while leaving force per length. It cannot produce whole-box force in N. Ranking 6,000 beside 2,500 would compare different quantities; dividing either figure into payload would add assumptions the replies do not support.

The CSV leaves method, edition, conditioning, direction and fittings blank because these fictional replies omit them. Even two board results need their actual methods and conditions checked. FEFCO separately describes board edge resistance and empty-container compression, with historical dates retained in its public booklet. These symbolic objects are not test apparatus. The filled-package question needs its own complete-system evidence and technical judgement; no safety factor or stack permission follows.

Keep checkpoints and revisions separate.

title: EXW and FCA Packaging Orders Need Different Pickup Arrangements
html:
For an overseas order of empty gift boxes, choose the intended pickup state before booking transport. Cartons available beside a vehicle, cartons loaded onto it and cartons arriving at a depot ready to unload describe different handovers. A freight quotation or a three-letter trade term does not show which operation the parties have arranged.

This guide uses hypothetical cartons and locations. It does not establish Packrivo’s contract terms, export capability or a completed shipment.

Compare the three delivery states

The ICC’s Incoterms 2020 rule text distinguishes these ordinary delivery conditions:

Arrangement Delivery condition Applicable export clearance
EXW at the agreed point Identified goods at the buyer’s disposal, not loaded Buyer, with the seller’s specified assistance
FCA at the seller’s premises Goods loaded onto buyer-provided transport Seller
FCA at another named place Goods on seller-provided transport, at the disposal of the buyer-nominated carrier or receiving person, ready to unload Seller

Risk normally follows the rule’s delivery event, subject to the contract and its exceptions. Buyer notice, nomination or collection failures can matter. Seller-assisted loading under EXW does not automatically change the agreed risk allocation; address that operation expressly. Under FCA elsewhere, seller unloading is not ordinarily required for delivery.

These are limited rule summaries. Read the applicable clauses with the responsible contracting and transport parties rather than treating the table as a complete Incoterms manual.

Describe the operation missing from the pickup instruction

Imagine four shipping cartons of empty jewelry boxes at a hypothetical warehouse. Their count, size and contents are unchanged in each proposal below.

For an EXW proposal, the dispatch contact identifies a release area where the cartons will be available. The buyer’s instruction says only that a driver will collect them. It has not explained who may enter the area, operate the equipment or put the cartons on the vehicle. Ask the site and transport contacts to resolve that work before confirming collection. A helpful warehouse worker and a driver with equipment are different operational proposals; neither should remain an undocumented assumption.

For an FCA seller-premises proposal, ask the dispatch contact to identify the loading bay and the vehicle the buyer will provide. A photograph of cartons waiting beside the bay locates the goods but leaves the loading event unanswered. Ask what record will show the intended handover state, including the cartons and collecting vehicle involved.

For an FCA depot proposal, identify the buyer-nominated carrier or receiving person as well as the destination point. The cartons arrive there on the seller’s vehicle. Ask the receiving contact how that arrival will be handled and who provides unloading. An appointment booking, an arrival photograph and a storage receipt issued later record different things; do not silently substitute one for another.

No warehouse, equipment, driver or depot has been verified for these examples. Their purpose is to expose the unanswered operation in each proposed collection plan.

Keep the event separate from its evidence

Give each retained photograph, notice or acknowledgment a factual description: cartons available at the release point, loading completed on the collecting vehicle, or arriving goods presented to the buyer-nominated carrier or receiving person ready for unloading. Record what the evidence actually shows and retain any missing fact.

A timestamp can help establish when an action occurred. A signature can identify an acknowledgment. Neither alone explains which contractual delivery condition was met. If the evidence and the agreed condition disagree, return the question to the responsible parties instead of renaming the record as delivered.

The carton freight-data guide supplies the separate count, dimensions and weight record. Those numbers help identify what travels; this review identifies the physical handover expected.

Resolve export capability and the wider agreement

Transport booking and lawful export arrangements need separate confirmation. Ask the party assigned the applicable formalities to explain its actual arrangement before committing to a pickup that depends on it. An unconfirmed contracting seller, exporter role or broker arrangement remains an open issue; writing a term on an invoice does not supply that authority.

The ICC’s contract-scope explanation distinguishes the rules from the wider sale contract. They do not determine ownership, payment terms, the legal imposition of tariffs or the law governing the contract. Local legal requirements and any specifically agreed variations still need review.

Use the quote comparison checklist for commercial scope. Attach a short pickup instruction that names the point, intended vehicle-related state, handling arrangement, applicable export responsibility and unresolved facts. The seller, buyer and receiving party should be able to recognize the same event from that instruction.

Sources checked 9 October 2026. The ICC pages identify the 2020 rules without a separate webpage revision date. This is packaging planning education, not a customs or contractual determination. Packrivo coordinates sourcing and project questions; actual delivery and export decisions remain with the contracting parties and their appropriate advisers. Any illustration is an AI-assisted concept.

Changing the named place changes which vehicle state matters

Keep the same invented carton lot L 1 while changing the proposed FCA place. BAY29 names the seller’s bay and buyer-provided vehicle V_B. DEPOT29 names a different receiving depot, seller-provided vehicle V_S and buyer-nominated receiver R_N. The carton identity can remain the same while the required vehicle-related delivery state changes. These tokens describe proposed roles, not dispatched goods or a completed handover.

Hypothetical configuration Named object Relationship Input or next scope
BAY29 BAY29 proposed place SELLER_BAY
BAY29 BAY29 proposed vehicle role BUYER_V_B
BAY29 BAY29 proposed delivery state LOADED_ON_BUYER_TRANSPORT
DEPOT29 DEPOT29 proposed place OTHER_NAMED_DEPOT
DEPOT29 DEPOT29 proposed vehicle role SELLER_V_S
DEPOT29 DEPOT29 proposed delivery state ARRIVED_READY_FOR_UNLOADING
DEPOT29 R_N is BUYER_NOMINATED_RECEIVER
PLACE_CHANGE29 BAY_LOADING_RECORD does not establish DEPOT_ARRIVAL
DEPOT29 ORDINARY_FCA_DELIVERY does not generally require SELLER_UNLOADING

For BAY29, a record showing L 1 loaded onto V_B addresses the ordinary seller-premises loading state. A photograph of L 1 beside that vehicle does not. For DEPOT29, the relevant ordinary state is L 1 arriving at the named depot on V_S, at the nominated receiver’s disposal, ready for unloading. A record that L 1 was loaded at the original warehouse does not establish arrival at the new named point. Seller unloading at the other place is not generally a condition of that ordinary FCA delivery event.

This prevents a document shortcut when the booking changes. Keep an existing bay-loading record under its original factual scope; do not rename it depot delivery. Identify the new destination point, nominated receiving person, arriving vehicle role and receiving arrangement. A later unloaded-storage receipt may be useful evidence of a different state, but it does not replace a factual account of the contractual event. No acknowledgment, actual appointment or risk transfer is invented in the download.

EXW remains another rule: goods at the agreed point available to the buyer, not ordinarily seller-loaded. Any proposed loading help needs its own arrangement. The ICC Incoterms 2020 rules also retain ordinary transport-packaging responsibilities under their stated conditions. A changed named place does not settle ownership, payment, tax responsibility or every contract variation. Use the carton-data record for what travels and this comparison for which operation the revised instruction must describe.

title: UK Packaging EPR and Plastic Tax Need Different Scope Checks
html:
Assess UK packaging EPR, Plastic Packaging Tax registration and component chargeability separately. EPR examines the responsible organisation and its packaging activities; Plastic Packaging Tax examines finished plastic components manufactured or imported by the relevant person. A recycled-plastic claim or a complete-carton weight cannot answer all three questions.

The comparison below is general packaging education. It does not determine a particular business’s reporting, registration or tax position.

Keep the responsible party and measurement basis distinct

The UK EPR eligibility guidance starts with packaging activities, UK establishment, relevant organisation or group, turnover and attributable packaging quantities. Activity-allocation rules determine which packaging the person must count.

HMRC’s Plastic Packaging Tax registration guidance starts with UK manufacture or import of finished plastic packaging components. It includes relevant components imported filled with goods and explains whose behalf an import is made on. Its responsible-person test cannot simply be replaced with the EPR brand-owner result.

Question UK packaging EPR Plastic Packaging Tax
Who needs assessment? The relevant UK-established organisation or group carrying out packaging activities The relevant manufacturer or importer of finished plastic components
What quantity is counted? Attributable packaging across the relevant materials and activities In-scope finished plastic components, with the applicable exclusion rules
Which time basis applies? The assessment year and packaging/accounts reference periods specified for EPR The rolling 12-month and expected next-30-day registration tests
What result is required? Organisational status and applicable producer responsibilities Registration position, then a separate chargeability result for each component

For a hypothetical brand buying finished empty boxes and plastic inserts from a UK supplier, that purchase alone does not make the brand the PPT manufacturer or importer. The supplier’s role and the brand’s own packaging activities still need review under their respective rules.

For a hypothetical import of already packed gifts, identify the party responsible for the import and the EPR allocation of each packaging item. A carrier or intermediary’s name on a document does not by itself settle every role. No real company or shipment is assumed in these examples.

Separate component weight from the recycled-plastic percentage

A paperboard box and a separately manufactured plastic insert should remain identifiable. Do not combine them with the goods into one carton-weight figure and use it for both regimes.

Under HMRC’s component-scope guidance, a mixed-material component is treated as plastic when plastic weighs more than each relevant other material. That test differs from simply asking whether plastic exceeds half of the total weight. The material groups and adhesive conditions in the guidance also matter.

Once the component’s scope is established, the recycled-plastic percentage uses qualifying recycled plastic divided by all plastic in that component. Non-plastic board or metal is not added to that percentage’s denominator. The whole component’s relevant weight and the plastic-content percentage therefore answer different questions.

Obtain the actual component specification and supported material weights. A supplier’s recycled-content wording without its basis cannot establish the tax calculation. The material-claim evidence guide helps identify what a document covers; it does not determine UK tax treatment.

Use the correct registration clock and preserve boundary questions

HMRC’s registration guide uses 10 tonnes or more of relevant finished plastic components manufactured or imported in the previous rolling 12 months, or expected in the next 30 days. The look-back test is made from the last day of the month; the forward test can apply when the expectation arises. Follow the guide’s liability-date and registration requirements rather than converting both tests into one calendar-year total.

EPR uses another basis. For its 2026 assessment guidance, Defra directs readers to packaging supplied or imported during 2025 and the specified accounts available before 7 April 2026. An eligibility reference period and the packaging-data period being reported must not be treated as interchangeable.

Regulation 24 of the 2024 EPR regulations uses “more than” turnover and packaging thresholds, with defined relative-year and group conditions. The government overview contains an inconsistent wording boundary around exactly £1 million. Keep a business at an exact boundary unresolved for review against the current regulations and relevant regulator guidance; this article does not resolve its classification from a summary table.

Every threshold record should identify the entity, applicable packaging, measurement period and source version. A box drawing contains none of the necessary organisational history or future manufacturing/import quantities by itself.

Non-chargeable components can still count for registration

HMRC’s component guidance states that plastic packaging with at least 30% qualifying recycled plastic is not chargeable on that basis, but still counts towards the applicable registration threshold. Retain evidence for the proportion and material source. This is why a supplier’s 30% statement cannot support a blanket no-registration conclusion.

HMRC also distinguishes tax exemptions from exclusions and does not treat them all identically for registration. The exemptions and exclusions guidance includes a conditional imported transport-packaging exemption. It must not be extended to every retail box or insert merely because the consignment travelled internationally.

Check the actual component and use. A plastic presentation insert and a separate outer transport component can need different treatments. The article has not established an exemption for either hypothetical item.

The component guide updated 28 August 2026 also announces a change to qualifying pre-consumer recycled plastic from 1 April 2027. That future change is not already effective on the 9 October 2026 review date. Keep production/import dates and the supporting source with any recycled-plastic record.

Close three outcomes with their own evidence

Keep an EPR organisational-status result, a PPT registration result and a PPT component-chargeability result. Record unresolved roles or weights in the specific investigation they affect.

If only a combined carton weight is available, request the component and material breakdown. If recycled content is unsupported, leave the relevant chargeability assumption open. If the organisation’s reference-year or group position is unknown, the packaging specification cannot close its EPR assessment.

Packrivo can help organize packaging specifications and supplier questions for the responsible UK business to review. This does not create a tax-advice, registration or regulatory-filing service.

Sources accessed 9 October 2026. EPR eligibility guidance was updated 19 August 2026; the cited PPT component guide was updated 28 August 2026 and registration guide 31 March 2023. Current legislation was read separately from government summaries; exact boundary and real-business applicability remain subject to the appropriate review. No accounts, tax amounts, return or registration were assessed or submitted. UK EPR is separate from EU PPWR. Any accompanying illustration is an AI-assisted concept.

A plastic minority can still be the heaviest material category

Use a separate invented component, MIX29, to test two different denominators. Assume it is a single finished component containing 40 g plastic, 35 g paper and 25 g metal, with the categories established on the relevant guidance basis and no separate adhesive question hidden in those figures. Its total is 100 g. Plastic is only 40% of the total, but 40 exceeds both 35 and 25. Under the stated HMRC material comparison, being below half of the total does not remove the plastic-component question.

Hypothetical configuration Named object Relationship Input or next scope

MIX29 PAPER assumed input 35 g
MIX29 METAL assumed input 25 g
MIX29 COMPONENT calculated from PLASTIC_MASS+PAPER_MASS+METAL_MASS; 100 g
MIX29 PLASTIC calculated from PLASTIC_MASS/TOTAL_MASS; 0.4 fraction
MIX29 QUALIFYING_RECYCLED_PLASTIC assumed input 12 g

EPR_A29 REG24_6_QUANTITY calculated from nearest_tonne(EPR_A29_RAW); 25 tonnes
EPR_B29 RELEVANT_QUANTITY assumed input 25.6 tonnes

Now assume 12 g of its 40 g plastic is qualifying recycled plastic under the applicable dated rules. The illustrative recycled-plastic fraction is 12 ÷ 40 = 30%, not 12 ÷ 100 = 12%. The non-plastic material does not belong in this fraction’s denominator. Recycled qualification, component scope and the actual evidence remain distinct. A hypothetical fraction at 30% supplies no actual non-chargeability decision; even an established non-chargeable component can still count for registration under the relevant rules.

EPR has a separate rounding issue. Regulation 24(6) requires the relevant packaging amount to be expressed to the nearest tonne. Assuming the correct relevant-year, organisation/group and allocation basis has first been established, invented amounts 25.4 tonnes and 25.6 tonnes become 25 and 26 tonnes respectively. Under a strict more-than-25-tonne quantity limb they land on different sides. This is only a quantity-limb illustration, not an organisational classification; neither raw 25.01 tonnes nor an overview table alone supplies the full answer.

The later source check actually obtained Regulation 24 and read its key clauses, while the earlier WebGPT access limitation remains part of the historical research record. The GOV.UK prose and table still differ around exact turnover and tonnage boundaries. Keep that discrepancy open rather than silently adding an equals sign. title: Empty Packaging Imports Need a Clear Origin-Marking Scope
html:
For empty packaging imported into the United States, identify the packaging’s origin, intended use and ultimate purchaser before deciding what must be marked. A brand importing boxes to fill and sell with its goods has a different fact pattern from a distributor reselling empty boxes. Any origin wording left visible after filling must identify its subject clearly.

This guide uses hypothetical arrangements. It does not determine the origin, classification or marking exception for an actual shipment.

Identify the imported article and its purchaser

Start with what crosses the border: the empty box, case, bag or other packaging component. Goods added after importation are not automatically part of that import. Under 19 CFR 134.1, origin concerns manufacture, production or growth, with additional processing rules. A departure point in China alone does not prove the origin of every component.

The same section defines the ultimate purchaser using the imported form and transaction conditions. It is not universally the importer of record. Identify who imports the boxes, who receives them as empty packaging, who fills them and whether they are resold individually or in bulk.

For a disposable-container arrangement covered by 134.24(c)(1), the importing business that fills the containers and sells the packaged goods can be the ultimate purchaser of those containers. A distributor that only resells empty boxes cannot assume it meets that filling-and-selling provision.

Match the marking route to the import and sale arrangement

The following branches are provisional. Physical construction, intended use, tariff treatment and any applicable exception still need review.

Hypothetical arrangement Marking question to resolve
A brand directly imports disposable empty boxes, then fills and sells them with its goods Does 134.24(c)(1) apply, and are the outside packages properly marked for the boxes’ origin?
A distributor imports disposable boxes and sells bulk packages to a separate filling business Under 134.24(b), which origin-marked outermost package reaches the identified ultimate purchaser?
Empty boxes are sold individually at retail How does the required origin information reach the purchaser of the empty packaging? A discarded wholesale carton is not an automatic substitute
Cases have independent lasting or decorative use Review 134.23 and actual classification before relying on disposable-container treatment
Packaging enters already filled with merchandise Review the origin of the contents and container under the applicable filled-import rules; do not carry over the empty-box conclusion
Use, purchaser or construction is unknown Hold the individual-versus-outer-package decision until those facts are identified

An outer carton can satisfy a particular route only under its conditions. For disposable containers sold in multiple units, 134.24(b) refers to the outermost package reaching the ultimate purchaser. A mark seen by a distributor before the boxes are divided may not describe the package the relevant purchaser receives.

Follow the boxes through any repacking

Imagine a distributor receives empty boxes in a marked master carton, then divides them into smaller groups for different filling businesses. These are hypothetical handling steps, not an observed shipment.

Draw the actual transfer path before relying on the master-carton mark. Identify each resulting package and its recipient. If the original carton stays at the distributor’s warehouse, it cannot simply be treated as the outermost carton delivered to the next purchaser.

19 CFR 134.26 addresses relevant repacking, certification and notification conditions. The importer should have its customs adviser review which requirements apply to the proposed arrangement. The article has not established an exception for any redistributed group of boxes.

This adds a purchaser-and-transfer question to the shipping record. The carton freight-data guide supplies count, size and weight; those figures do not establish a marking exception.

Reuse and usual-container treatment need their actual conditions

Do not classify every sturdy gift box as reusable or every paperboard box as disposable. 134.22(d) explains usual-container treatment and notes that sturdiness and repeated use with the contents do not alone exclude a container from that category.

Independent lasting value, decorative use and how the item is entered and sold can raise different questions. Section 134.23 refers to the relevant tariff interpretation rules; the buyer must not assign that treatment from a photo or a supplier’s premium-box description.

An empty fitted case is also not automatically given the same tariff treatment as a case imported with its intended contents. Provide the actual imported condition and intended use to the responsible classification reviewer.

Keep the box’s origin separate from the goods inside

Suppose an empty box has a verified Chinese origin and will later hold goods whose origin is not established. This assumption is only for the example; no real box or product origin has been verified here.

Section 134.24(c)(2) requires a visible origin mark on relevant individually marked containers imported for filling to identify the container rather than the contents. A hypothetical statement such as “Container made in China” describes the assumed box origin. It is not print-ready approved wording or a conclusion that every such box needs an individual mark.

An unqualified origin statement on a filled gift presentation can suggest that the contents share the box’s origin. Filling a box in the United States does not establish that the contents were made there either. The two origin decisions need their own facts.

If geographic wording or a US address appears, include it in the responsible review of the applicable marking provisions. An address is not proof of manufacture, but the article does not classify every address printed on empty packaging as a violation.

Once the origin and marking subject are resolved, the retail-copy responsibility guide can keep the approved words connected to the artwork. The proof should show the actual location and the final presentation after filling, alongside any outer-package marking relied upon.

Sources checked 9 October 2026. The cited eCFR pages displayed Title 19 current through dates from 1 to 7 October 2026; the text is authoritative but an unofficial electronic edition. These branches do not assign a tariff code, establish origin, approve a marking exception or authorize a US-origin claim. Packrivo coordinates packaging information; customs classification and transaction-specific decisions remain with the importing business and its appropriate advisers. Any accompanying illustration is an AI-assisted concept.

A mark on a master carton does not travel with every split group

Draw a separate invented redistribution record. SPLIT28 starts with twenty empty boxes in MASTER_M1 at distributor D. The distributor divides them into GROUP_A and GROUP_B, ten boxes each, for two filling businesses. The master carton stays at D. These numbers describe a transfer example; actual origin, container category, ultimate purchaser and marking treatment remain unknown.

Hypothetical configuration Named object Relationship Input or next scope
SPLIT28 MASTER_M1 assumed quantity 20 empty boxes
SPLIT28 GROUP_A assumed quantity 10 empty boxes
SPLIT28 GROUP_B assumed quantity 10 empty boxes
SPLIT28 GROUP_A_PLUS_GROUP_B calculated from GROUP_A_COUNT+GROUP_B_COUNT; 20 empty boxes
SPLIT28 MASTER_M1 assumed remains at DISTRIBUTOR_D
SPLIT28 GROUP_A assumed received by FILLING_BUSINESS_A
SPLIT28 GROUP_B assumed received by FILLING_BUSINESS_B
SPLIT28 M1_MARK does not by itself establish ORIGIN_INFO_ON_GROUP_A_OR_GROUP_B
DIRECT28 UNSPLIT_MASTER assumed reaches DIRECT_IMPORTER_FILLER
BOTH28 RECIPIENT_ROLE does not automatically assign ULTIMATE_PURCHASER_OR_MARKING_EXCEPTION
FILLED_LATER28 CONTAINER_ORIGIN does not establish CONTENTS_ORIGIN
BOTH28 ORIGIN_WORDING status PENDING_NO_PRINT_READY_APPROVED_STATEMENT

The count reconciles: ten plus ten equals twenty empty boxes. That does not reconcile the origin-information path. A mark remaining on M1 cannot by itself establish what reaches either recipient after the groups leave separately. Identify the package each relevant purchaser actually receives, and ask the customs reviewer which marking, repacking and notification conditions apply. Do not turn an outer mark once seen at the warehouse into a blanket exception for every subsequent package.

DIRECT28 is a different premise: an unsplit master reaches a direct importer-filler. The section 134.24(c)(1) route still depends on the actual qualifying container, filling-and-selling relationship and outside-package marking conditions. The split distributor example cannot borrow those facts merely because its customers intend to fill boxes. A recipient’s role also does not automatically settle who is the ultimate purchaser under the actual import arrangement.

Keep individual empty-box retail, independently lasting or decorative containers, and already-filled imports on their separate branches. Section 134.26 has defined repacking conditions and exceptions; this worksheet assigns neither a universal certification requirement nor an exemption. After filling, any applicable visible container-origin statement must have its proper subject. Container origin does not establish the goods’ origin, and no print-ready country statement is supplied here. Carry the actual route, construction and proposed final presentation to the importer’s appropriate adviser before artwork is finalized.

Actual quantity, configuration, component and file identities, materials, process, specification, copy, method, condition, observation, owner, decision, evidence and dates are blank. ACTUAL_BLANK is a separate empty starting row; enter permitted project evidence before using an actual record. A blank means unknown.

Use the Packaging Freight Quotes: Carton Data to Prepare for its separate question. Use the Assign Product Copy Responsibility Before the Packaging Proof for its separate question.

title: Magnetic Gift Boxes Need an Air-Shipment Review
html:
A magnetic gift-box closure and the outer carton offered for air transport need different reviews. The closure’s opening feel does not establish the external magnetic field of a carton holding many boxes. Identify the complete shipping configuration, obtain appropriate technical evidence and check the intended air service before describing the shipment as ready to fly.

This article explains those decision boundaries. It does not classify or approve an actual gift-box shipment, prescribe a magnetic measurement method or supply a shipping label.

Define the shipping package rather than one closure

A magnet specification describes one component. The air-shipment review concerns the final packed package. Identify the closure construction, number and arrangement of boxes, their flat or assembled state, the outer carton and any other included components.

Keep that configuration tied to its version. Evidence from one retail box cannot simply be renamed as a result for a master carton. Nor should a buyer multiply a single-magnet figure by the box count and treat the result as a measured package field.

For a collapsible design, compare the specified delivery state with the state the shipping party will actually offer. The folding gift-box guide covers closure and assembly questions; it does not answer the magnetic air-transport question.

The US prohibition is a package-level condition

49 CFR 173.21(d) forbids carriage by aircraft of a package with a magnetic field greater than 0.00525 gauss measured at 4.5 m, or 15 feet, from any surface of the package. The stated relation is greater than; do not change it to a different cutoff or distance.

That provision concerns the package offered for transport. It is not a specification for choosing a retail-box magnet. A photograph, closure-force statement or successful opening trial cannot provide the field evidence it requires.

The FAA’s Advisory Circular 121-28, issued in 1987 and listed as active at review, explains the aircraft compass-interference concern. It uses an older paragraph reference; cite the current 173.21(d) for the US prohibition rather than carrying the advisory’s old numbering into a new brief.

A result that does not trigger this prohibition still leaves other applicable transport and acceptance questions open. Do not turn one numerical screen into an international shipping guarantee.

Check international rules and the actual cargo service separately

ICAO’s Technical Instructions page identifies the 2025–2026 edition for operations through 31 December 2026. IATA’s 2026 publication information identifies its 67th Dangerous Goods Regulations edition. These edition pages are not the complete technical requirements.

A historical PHMSA interpretation distinguishes US HMR treatment from international magnetized-material provisions. It is useful context, not a substitute for the applicable current text. The responsible shipping party needs the relevant international criteria, variations and operator instructions for the actual route.

Carrier acceptance is another decision. DHL Aviation Cargo’s commodity page lists magnetized material and states that special-cargo acceptance depends on the operator and destination, with prior approval required. That is a cargo-service example, not permission for any DHL courier product or a particular China-origin shipment.

Passenger guidance about carrying magnets in baggage also cannot settle acceptance of a commercial packaging order.

Give missing evidence and adverse findings different outcomes

The following are planning states, not results from a tested package.

Situation for the defined shipping configuration Appropriate decision
No suitable field evidence exists Hold the air-eligibility statement and obtain an appropriate technical assessment
The evidence exceeds the applicable US prohibition Stop the air-carriage proposal where this US prohibition applies and return it to qualified transport review; special-cargo acceptance does not override the prohibition
The prohibition does not stop it, but applicable rules require a magnetized-material route Resolve the current classification, handling and operator arrangements with the responsible shipper
A qualified review supports a non-restricted proposal under the applicable rules Present the correctly described package to the chosen service for route-specific acceptance
The intended operator declines or does not offer the required service Resolve another appropriate service or transport proposal; a technical result does not compel acceptance

The article has not acquired the complete current ICAO/IATA provisions. It therefore supplies no international numerical classification cutoff, procedure, marking instruction or automatic general-cargo decision.

Keep a hypothetical master carton on hold until it is assessed

Imagine a gift brand plans to ship empty magnetic-closure boxes together in master cartons. It has product images, proposed carton counts and a freight estimate, but no suitable magnetic-field evidence.

The immediate output is an identified packing configuration with air eligibility unresolved. Give the responsible shipping party the confirmed closure construction, delivered state, boxes per carton, arrangement and outer-pack specification. Ask what assessment and evidence the actual air route requires. Disclose the magnetic closures rather than assuming an ordinary freight quotation has already considered them.

The qualified evaluator determines the appropriate instrumentation, method and interpretation. This guide does not recommend improvised shielding or magnet repositioning as a proven solution. A visual arrangement can identify the proposal; it cannot establish the field.

If the closure, box count, delivery state or carton arrangement changes, ask whether the earlier evidence still covers that package. If the carrier or route changes while the physical package stays the same, reopen the acceptance question separately.

The carton freight-data worksheet helps identify the shipping units. A protection or distribution test answers another question and does not itself establish magnetic-field compliance. Packrivo can coordinate packaging specifications and supplier questions; the technical and shipping decisions remain with the appropriate responsible parties.

Sources reviewed 9 October 2026. The eCFR page displayed Title 49 current through 6 October 2026; the FAA advisory retains its 1987 issue date. ICAO/IATA edition information and DHL’s public cargo description do not provide full current technical provisions or shipment-specific acceptance. No package measurement, qualified laboratory result or carrier approval is claimed. Any accompanying illustration is an AI-assisted concept.

A published future edition does not cover a changed package or route

Compare three invented packed-package records without assigning a magnetic field. PACK_A28 contains twelve boxes in a flat delivery state. PACK_B28 also contains twelve but in an assembled state. PACK_C28 contains twenty-four flat boxes. Arrangement, outer packing, closure construction and suitable field evidence remain actual unknowns. The numbers define comparison scope, not a safe packing density or an air-shipping offer.

PACK_A28 MAGNETIC_BOX assumed delivery state FLAT
PACK_B28 MAGNETIC_BOX assumed pack count 12 boxes/package
PACK_B28 MAGNETIC_BOX assumed delivery state ASSEMBLED
PACK_C28 MAGNETIC_BOX assumed pack count 24 boxes/package
PACK_C28 MAGNETIC_BOX assumed delivery state FLAT

DATE_SCOPE28 SHIPMENT_D1 hypothetical operation date 2026-10-17
DATE_SCOPE28 SHIPMENT_D2 hypothetical operation date 2027-01-02

A result for one package cannot simply transfer to either changed state. Nor can a single-box figure be multiplied by twelve or twenty-four to create a measured external field for the packed carton. Ask the qualified evaluator what evidence covers the exact offered arrangement. The current US clause uses strictly greater than 0.00525 gauss at 4.5 m from any package surface; this source reference supplies no measurement procedure, actual field result or automatic clearance at or below the number.

Keep the operation date on another axis. The original ICAO 2025–2026 and IATA 2026/67th edition references remain correct within their stated scope. IATA announced publication of its 2027 manuals on 7 September 2026, while its update page identifies the 2027/68th DGR as effective from 1 January 2027. A hypothetical operation on 17 October 2026 and another on 2 January 2027 therefore need their appropriate edition, addenda and applicability review; publication alone does not make the future edition operative in October.

Changing the operator or service reopens acceptance even if the physical package stays unchanged. DHL Aviation Cargo’s public category description is not approval by every DHL courier product or for this shipment. Full current ICAO/IATA technical provisions were not acquired, and no international numerical cutoff, handling procedure, shielding solution or label is prescribed. Leave air eligibility pending until qualified technical and shipping reviewers resolve the actual package, applicable rules and chosen route.

title: Braille Packaging Needs Transcription and Tactile Reading Checks
html:
Braille on gift packaging needs two kinds of evidence: the raised information must represent the intended message correctly, and its physical reproduction must be readable by touch. A dot-shaped font or an embossed decorative pattern cannot establish either result.

For a brand exploring this option, first identify the information a braille reader needs. Then obtain a code-specific transcription review and a physical reading proof. The example below is hypothetical; no braille artwork, sample or reader evaluation has been produced.

Give written information a different job from an opening cue

An embossed logo can provide decoration. A tactile marker can help a customer find a pull tab. Braille communicates linguistic information. State which job the feature is intended to perform before choosing its production method.

The accessible gift-packaging guide addresses locating, gripping, opening and removing the gift. Those actions do not establish that a raised product identifier conveys correct words or numbers.

Braille also serves people who read it. Ask the intended users which information routes help them; a braille feature alone does not address every blind or partially sighted recipient’s needs.

Keep the print message and braille code identifiable

Suppose a brand wants the hypothetical identifier “Candle Gift Set 02” on its carton in braille. The brand must approve that exact message before transcription. The identifier is an example, not a real product or approved braille string.

Check source characters carefully. RNIB’s transcription guidance identifies errors such as using a letter in place of a numeral or a superscript zero instead of the proper degree symbol. A visually similar source character can give the transcription process the wrong input.

Name the reading language and ask a qualified transcriber which code and contracted or uncontracted approach fit the message. For English, the International Council on English Braille publishes the Rules of Unified English Braille, Third Edition, 2024. Its numeric mode and contraction rules require more than replacing each print character with a dot-shaped character.

“Set 02” therefore needs a code-specific review of the letters and number. Do not select contracted braille merely to squeeze the message onto a small panel. The transcriber should resolve that choice for the intended content and readers. UEB does not replace the braille code required for a different reading language.

A braille font is a display tool, not transcription approval

RNIB’s braille-font guidance warns that changing an ordinary print font to a braille font can produce incorrect numbers or contracted braille. It distinguishes simulated on-screen dots from a method that produces raised braille.

Ask the qualified reviewer to compare the transcribed message with the approved print source using an appropriate braille representation or reading medium. Retain the language, code, edition, contraction decision, source revision and accepted transcription file. If software is used, keep its relevant version and transcription-table identity with the record.

The brand can request this evidence without claiming to read braille itself. An apparently plausible Unicode string or screenshot should remain a reference until the appropriate content review is complete. RNIB also notes that rule updates and software updates may occur at different times.

Evaluate the intended raised reading surface

A correctly transcribed message still needs suitable physical reproduction. Ask the proposed producer to identify the offered surface and process, then prepare a proof or sample representing that packaging construction. A screen enlargement cannot show what a finger will encounter.

With appropriate specialist input and relevant braille readers, examine whether the feature can be found, whether its information can be followed by touch and whether adjacent relief, folds or components interfere. Record the configuration and what was actually observed. These are project planning questions, not a prescribed test method or certification result.

The transcriber may need to check the produced copy for content or reproduction errors as well. Keep that code review distinct from feedback about finding and reading the feature during use.

RNIB’s font page gives a size example for a particular swell-paper application. It is not a universal dot-size requirement for gift boxes or labels. Obtain physical specifications from the appropriate specialist and proposed process; this guide supplies no manufacturing dimensions or tolerances.

Match each error to the decision it changes

Evidence or issue Decision to reopen
The brand changes “Set 02” to “Set 03” Review the revised source and its transcription; the old number approval does not cover it
Numbers or contractions were produced by a simple font change Obtain code-specific transcription and proofreading before accepting the content
Correct content exists only as a screen image Keep physical readability unresolved; request the appropriate raised proof
The produced message is difficult to locate or follow Review the position, surrounding features and physical production, then evaluate the revised configuration
A raised opening marker is labeled as braille Identify it as an action cue; initiate transcription only if written information is required

For the hypothetical carton, accepting the print message closes only the source-wording decision. The braille code choice, reviewed transcription and physical reading evidence remain open. Moving an accepted message to another panel can reopen physical reading conditions even when its wording stays the same.

Bring the message, reading language, proposed packaging surface and unresolved specialist questions to the packaging brief. Packrivo can coordinate those packaging questions; the qualified transcriber, producer and relevant readers provide their respective evidence. No braille production, specialist capacity or accessibility certification service is established by this article.

Sources accessed 9 October 2026. RNIB’s cited pages display no publication date; the ICEB page identifies the 2024 rulebook and later technical guidance updates. The short identifier and review sequence are hypothetical editorial planning aids. No transcription, physical proof, user study or legal accessibility conclusion has been approved here. Any accompanying illustration is an AI-assisted concept and must not be used as braille artwork.

A changed number and a moved message reopen different evidence

Use print text only to compare three hypothetical requests. BASE28 names “Candle Gift Set 02” on PANEL_A. COPY_CHANGE28 substitutes “Candle Gift Set 03” on that panel. MOVE_ONLY28 retains the Set 02 wording but proposes PANEL_B. These are source and location tokens, not approved wording, transcribed braille or produced packaging.

title: Wooden Shipping Supports Need a Material-Scope Check
html:
For packaging goods shipped from China to the continental United States, identify the material and role of every wooden part before selecting its import-review route. A plywood deck does not establish that the support blocks beneath it are processed wood. Wooden boxes imported as merchandise also need a separate review from the pallet carrying them.

This guide uses hypothetical constructions. It organizes material-scope questions for the packing party and importer; it does not establish treatment, mark authorization or compliance for an actual shipment.

Read the supporting assembly before accepting its name

The IPPC’s ISPM 15 publication concerns raw-wood packaging used to support, protect or carry goods in international trade, including dunnage. Its processed-wood exclusion is construction-specific.

List the deck, blocks, feet, runners, braces and loose supports separately. For each part, obtain the material and manufacturing description from the packing party. A photograph or sales term such as plywood pallet cannot identify concealed parts.

In section 2.1 of the official 2018 adopted, 2019 published text, the processed-wood exemption applies to packaging made wholly from qualifying processed material. A support with a plywood face and raw solid-wood blocks does not meet that whole-assembly condition.

The section also contains other conditional exceptions. Do not infer that an assembly qualifies because one part meets an exception, or because a decorative wooden box looks finished. The table below records investigation routes rather than import approvals.

Compare material, role and route together

Every row assumes the stated material has been confirmed. Unknown material belongs in the last row.

Hypothetical construction Function on the China-to-US route Scope decision to carry forward
Raw solid-wood pallet or braces outside the relevant exceptions Supports or protects cartons Regulated WPM review under the applicable US requirements
Support made wholly from verified qualifying processed plywood, including its feet and runners Carries cartons Document the complete construction for the section 2.1 processed-wood exemption review
Plywood deck with raw solid-wood blocks outside the relevant exceptions Carries cartons Review the solid-wood parts and complete assembly as regulated WPM; do not claim the wholly processed-wood exemption
Empty wooden gift boxes imported for resale Merchandise itself Separate wood-product import review for the actual construction and classification
Wooden gift box holding another imported item Packaging function Review the specific gift-box exception and its processing condition; the category name is insufficient
Separate pallet carrying wooden gift-box merchandise Transport support Assess its own constituent materials independently of the boxes
Support sold as wooden or plywood, with unspecified feet or blocks Proposed transport support Hold the material classification until the full construction is identified

APHIS’s US wood-packaging importer guidance, modified 27 July 2026, is the destination-market starting point. It describes regulated WPM and lists processed-material alternatives. Those alternatives concern transport packaging; they do not clear the merchandise itself for import.

Resolve a mixed or unknown support before packing approval

Consider a hypothetical proposal for a plywood deck. The drawing identifies its surface but leaves the support blocks unnamed. Record the proposal as unresolved rather than treating the visible plywood as evidence for the complete assembly.

If the packing party identifies the blocks as raw solid wood outside the relevant exceptions, move the assembly into regulated-WPM review. If all supporting members are confirmed as qualifying processed material, retain that component evidence with the proposed exemption route. Neither outcome comes from an appearance comparison.

For the regulated route, the importer and exporter must establish who provides the applicable compliant WPM and how the actual support will be reviewed before dispatch. Treatment and official marking operate under the relevant national plant protection organization’s authority. A designer-generated mark or unverified supplier statement cannot establish that authority.

When the material remains unknown, request the missing construction, consider a fully specified alternative or ask the importer to obtain the appropriate official guidance. Do not convert missing information into a declaration that customs has rejected the support.

Keep merchandise requirements beside the support review

ISPM 15’s gift-box exception depends on processing or manufacture that renders the material free from pests. Its accompanying footnote warns that some gift boxes remain within scope. A smooth exterior or decorative finish alone cannot prove that condition.

When the boxes themselves are imported goods, the importer needs their origin, materials, construction, finish, use and commodity classification. APHIS’s plant-material requirements page identifies wood-containing handicrafts from China, including boxes, as a category requiring attention. Its generally authorized products page describes qualifying finished constructions. Read the applicable conditions together rather than treating either page as a universal answer.

The importer can use APHIS’s commodity requirements database for the actual goods. Lacey Act declaration requirements are another distinct check: the page separates packaging used to carry other goods from packaging imported as merchandise, and includes classification and entry conditions. This article does not assign a tariff code or filing result to a gift box.

Add a material-scope record to the freight description

For each support or wood commodity, retain its identity, role, component materials, evidence and open decision. Name the packing or importing party that will close the question. A practical hypothetical entry is:

P-03: plywood deck with raw solid-wood blocks outside the relevant exceptions. Transport support. The wholly processed-wood condition is not met. Importer and exporter to resolve the regulated-WPM arrangement before packing approval.

Keep that record with the carton configuration and revision. The carton freight-data worksheet supplies count, dimensions and weight; it does not replace this material-scope review. Reopen the scope record when a supplier changes a deck, foot, runner or brace.

Packrivo can help organize packaging specifications and coordinate the material questions. The relevant packing party, importer and authorities confirm the requirements for the actual shipment.

Sources checked 9 October 2026. The IPPC adopted-standards index was observed with its ISPM 15 entry pointing to publication 640. The readable text used here was adopted in 2018 and published in 2019; the adopted list updated 25 March 2026 records those annex revisions. The index’s English FAO download returned a reading restriction, so no byte-for-byte latest-edition guarantee is made. No actual support, treatment or shipment was inspected. Any accompanying illustration is an AI-assisted concept.

One unknown foot keeps the whole-material conclusion open

Name every supporting member in a separate invented assembly: deck D1, runner R1 and foot F1. Assume D1 and R1 are qualifying processed plywood. UNKNOWN28 leaves F1’s material unknown; RAW_BLOCK28 specifies raw solid wood outside the relevant exceptions; PROCESSED28 assumes F1 is qualifying processed plywood too. Each assembly is a transport support, not the wooden gift-box merchandise it may carry.

Hypothetical configuration Named object Relationship Input or next scope
UNKNOWN28 DECK_D1 assumed material QUALIFYING_PROCESSED_PLYWOOD
UNKNOWN28 RUNNER_R1 assumed material QUALIFYING_PROCESSED_PLYWOOD
UNKNOWN28 FOOT_F1 assumed material UNKNOWN
UNKNOWN28 FOOT_F1 prevents conclusion WHOLLY_PROCESSED_SCOPE
RAW_BLOCK28 FOOT_F1 assumed material RAW_SOLID_WOOD_OUTSIDE_RELEVANT_EXCEPTIONS
RAW_BLOCK28 ASSEMBLY_A1 does not meet WHOLLY_QUALIFYING_PROCESSED_CONDITION
PROCESSED28 FOOT_F1 assumed material QUALIFYING_PROCESSED_PLYWOOD
PROCESSED28 ASSEMBLY_A1 supplies assumed basis for SECTION_2_1_EXCLUSION_REVIEW
GOODS28 GIFT_BOX_G1 requires separate WOOD_PRODUCT_IMPORT_AND_LACEY_APPLICABILITY
GOODS28 SUPPORT_SCOPE does not clear GIFT_BOX_MERCHANDISE
GOODS28 ACIR_REQUIREMENTS status NOT_QUERIED_TOOL_ACCESS_GAP_NOT_404

UNKNOWN28 has no basis for a wholly processed-material conclusion. RAW_BLOCK28 does not meet that condition and needs the applicable regulated-WPM review; that is not a finding that a shipment has been rejected. PROCESSED28 supplies an assumed complete-construction basis for the section 2.1 exclusion review. It is still no actual exemption or import clearance, because none of those component descriptions has been verified for a real support.

Apply the word wholly to the complete construction, including any additional feet, runners, braces or loose supports the actual arrangement uses. A plywood deck photograph cannot fill an unknown block field. The ISPM 15 text used for the source review was adopted in 2018 and published in 2019; an index-page date is not a new technical edition. Official marking and treatment authority remain distinct from a design description.

Keep wooden gift boxes imported as merchandise on their own record. The support’s material scope cannot settle the goods’ plant-material requirements, classification, origin or Lacey applicability. No actual ACIR commodity query was run; the reported internal access error is not a demonstrated 404 or a conclusion about the goods. Give the importer the actual full construction, role and entry facts instead of translating a transport-support exclusion into a general wood-product import permission.

Download the wood packaging support all component material scope record (.csv). It includes the original table fields and scenarios alongside the added relationships. HYPOTHETICAL rows are editorial examples or required review scopes, not actual records. Actual quantity, configuration, component and file identities, materials, process, specification, copy, method, condition, observation, owner, decision, evidence and dates are blank. ACTUAL_BLANK is a separate empty starting row; enter permitted project evidence before using an actual record. A blank means unknown.

Use the Packaging Freight Quotes: Carton Data to Prepare for its separate question.

APHIS transport WPM, merchandise plant-material and Lacey requirements remain separate. ACIR had an internal retrieval error, not a verified 404; no actual commodity query or import decision occurred. The added configurations and calculations are hypothetical, with actual evidence and decisions pending.

title: Mixed-Material Gift Packaging Needs a Component Disposal Map
html:
Write disposal instructions for the components a customer will have after opening the gift. Identify what separates by hand, what stays attached and which local household program accepts each final state. A paperboard box, loose film and ribbon can need different instructions even when they arrive as one package.

The example below uses San Francisco household guidance. It is a hypothetical planning tool, not an instruction approved for a real product or a rule for other destinations.

Define the package before writing the removal steps

Assume a gift arrives in an ordinary non-waxed cardboard box with a separate plain, non-metallic paper band, a hand-tied ribbon and a loose plastic film sheet. The band slides away, the ribbon unties and the film can be lifted out. These construction assumptions must be checked on any actual design.

Keep the loose film distinct from a film laminated to the cardboard. A bonded layer, glued decoration or unidentified coating changes the remaining component. Gloss, color or a supplier’s broad paper description cannot settle that construction.

For this example, the paper and cardboard must also be clean and dry when discarded. No insert, jar, product or other accessory is included in the map; each additional item would need its own applicable review.

Make the intended sequence produce identifiable components

  1. Untie the ribbon and set it aside. It can be kept for another use; if discarded, it needs its own route.
  2. Slide the plain paper band off the box. Keep it separate from the ribbon.
  3. Remove the gift, then lift out the loose plastic film. This action describes a separate sheet, not peeling a laminate from board.
  4. Empty and flatten the cardboard box. Check the state of the cardboard before assigning its route.

These are proposed hand actions. Before adapting the sequence to customer-facing copy, try the actual construction and record any step that leaves an attachment behind or requires a different action. The concept illustration will not demonstrate that removal works.

Map each final state to San Francisco household guidance

Recology’s San Francisco three-cart guide describes its accepted paper/cardboard states and lists plastic bags and film under landfill items. SF Environment’s cardboard entry adds preparation and contamination conditions. Apply those conditions to the separated item rather than to the assembled gift box.

Final state in this hypothetical package Preparation or condition Household route supported by the cited guidance
Untied ribbon Kept for reuse or discarded separately If discarded, landfill; the city’s 29 December 2025 notice names ribbon and twine
Separate plain, non-metallic paper band Clean, dry and still the specified plain paper Blue recycling cart under the paper guidance
Loose plastic film Removed as a separate sheet Landfill under the cited three-cart guide
Ordinary non-waxed cardboard box Empty, clean, dry and flattened Blue recycling cart; wet or food/grease-contaminated cardboard is excluded
Attached or unidentified layer Construction or remaining state unresolved No cart assigned by this example; identify the component and resolve its specific route

The cardboard entry allows clean portions to be separated from soiled portions. That does not establish a method for stripping an unidentified coating or laminate.

Use the household guide specified here. A commercial-customer FAQ gives different plastic-bag preparation advice. It does not establish a household route for this loose-film example. Recheck the relevant service guidance before finalizing actual customer instructions; no collection-provider clarification has been obtained for this article.

The December 2025 city notice also described temporary tree and light collection windows. Those January 2026 arrangements have expired and are not disposal options recommended here.

Hold the unknown component without blocking the known ones

Suppose a glossy surface remains after the loose film is removed. Keep the connected component together while the brand resolves its construction. Do not instruct the customer to scrape, heat or peel an unknown layer. Already separated components can retain their independently supported routes.

The brand needs the substrate, finish, film or coating and attachment method for the affected face. The surface-layer BOM guide explains how to obtain those details. Then prepare an item-specific question containing the component, material, attached state and disposal location for Recology’s WhatBin resource.

If the exact state still has no confirmed route, keep its instruction pending. This example has not established acceptance for any glued or coated gift-box assembly, and an unknown component does not automatically receive a landfill assignment.

Turn the map into construction-specific copy

For the defined example, proposed wording could read:

For San Francisco households: untie the ribbon and place it in the landfill cart if discarded. Slide off the plain paper band and recycle it if clean and dry. Lift out the loose plastic film and place it in the landfill cart. Empty and flatten the clean, dry, non-waxed cardboard box for the blue recycling cart.

This is hypothetical planning copy. It depends on the four specified components, successful separation and the named household program. Keep the package revision, removal sequence, final states and source dates beside the proposed wording. Reopen the map if the material, attachment or destination changes.

Environmental wording for the complete package requires its own review. The material-claim evidence guide covers that broader question; this disposal map does not authorize a package-wide recyclable claim or recycling symbol.

Sources checked 9 October 2026. The cardboard and three-cart pages show no publication date; the ribbon notice is dated 29 December 2025. No real package, removal test, recycling outcome or collection agreement is established here. Any accompanying illustration is an AI-assisted concept.

A bonded-film revision changes the remaining component

Compare two invented revisions before carrying disposal copy forward. LOOSE28 has the original separate film sheet, plain paper band and untied ribbon. Its ordinary non-waxed board is assumed empty, clean, dry and flattened at disposal. BONDED28 instead attaches film F1 to board C1. The band and ribbon remain separately removable in this example; the board-and-film remainder has changed.

Hypothetical configuration Named object Relationship Input or next scope
LOOSE28 FILM_F1 assumed attachment SEPARATE_LOOSE_SHEET
BONDED28 FILM_F1 assumed attachment BONDED_FILM_ON_BOARD
LOOSE28 BOARD_C1 assumed final state EMPTY_CLEAN_DRY_NONWAXED_FLATTENED
LOOSE28 BOARD_C1 source limited household route SF_BLUE_CART_IF_STATED_CONDITIONS_MET
LOOSE28 FILM_F1 source limited household route SF_LANDFILL_IF_DISCARDED
BONDED28 BOARD_C1_WITH_FILM_F1 requires COMPOSITE_CONSTRUCTION_AND_ACTUAL_ROUTE
BONDED28 BONDED_LAYER has no authorized method HEAT_SCRAPE_OR_PEEL
BOTH28 BAND_B1 retains limited route scope SF_PLAIN_PAPER_IF_CLEAN_DRY_AND_ACCEPTED
BOTH28 RIBBON_R1 retains limited route scope KEEP_FOR_REUSE_OR_RECHECK_DISCARD_ROUTE
BOTH28 SEPARATE_COMPONENT_ROUTES do not authorize WHOLE_PACKAGE_RECYCLABLE_CLAIM

For the specified loose-sheet state, the cited San Francisco household guidance supplies a limited route for film discarded separately and for qualifying prepared cardboard. It does not answer the bonded composite. Keep BOARD_C1_WITH_FILM_F1 as one unresolved state until the real construction and service guidance are established. No scraping, heating or peeling method is proposed or shown as successful.

Avoid reopening unrelated components merely because one attachment changed. The plain band still needs its stated clean, dry material and household acceptance conditions; the ribbon can be retained for another use, with any discard instruction rechecked for the current local route. Neither component’s record makes the attached board recyclable. Conversely, an unresolved composite does not erase separately supported information about the unaffected items.

The household/commercial distinction remains important. A commercial bag preparation instruction cannot approve a household loose-film route. The city notice dated 29 December 2025 is a historical source for ribbon and twine; its January 2026 tree and light collection windows are not current service options. This revision map supports item-specific copy review for a named household location. It authorizes neither a whole-package recyclable claim nor a universal cart assignment.

Actual quantity, configuration, component and file identities, materials, process, specification, copy, method, condition, observation, owner, decision, evidence and dates are blank. ACTUAL_BLANK is a separate empty starting row; enter permitted project evidence before using an actual record. A blank means unknown.

Use the Lamination and Varnish Need Separate Layers in the Packaging BOM for its separate question. Use the Packaging Material Claims: Match the Evidence Scope for its separate question.

The 29 December 2025 holiday announcement is historical, and its January 2026 collection windows have passed. The added configurations and calculations are hypothetical, with actual evidence and decisions pending.
