title: Confirm Barcode Data Before Sending the Artwork
html:
Confirm barcode source data with its responsible owner before placing a generated symbol into packaging artwork. Record the product identity, intended use, data version and artwork file together. Compare the decoded content with the approved source; a successful scan alone doesn’t establish correct data or printed-symbol quality.

Artwork work can move quickly once an image exists. The harder question is whether that image represents the right product and intended data. Establish the source record before the designer treats the symbol as a fixed visual element.

Identify who owns the data and its use

GS1’s retail 2D implementation guidance, release 1.1.0 ratified in December 2025, discusses selecting data with stakeholders and separately reviews barcode quality. Use the appropriate current guidance with the brand’s responsible barcode specialist. This worksheet does not prescribe a symbol type for every retail channel.

Record the product or trade-item identity and the intended scanning use. A retail unit, outer carton and consumer-information link can have different requirements. Ask the responsible owner to confirm which one this artwork carries.

Keep identifiers as exact strings in the handoff record. Preserve any leading characters required by the source. Avoid retyping data from a screenshot or asking an image generator to invent a barcode.

If the source data is unavailable, mark the artwork location as pending and keep a clearly labelled non-production placeholder in the working file. A realistic-looking invented symbol should not become the production handoff.

Trace the source through generation and artwork

Save the approved source version and identify the file generated from it. Record the tool or responsible service used to generate the symbol and the stated configuration. Keep that record separate from the designer’s placement decision.

Compare the decoded content from the generated symbol with the approved source using a suitable agreed method. Record the actual result and any mismatch. A visual inspection of the bars or squares cannot settle the encoded data.

Then identify the artwork file and revision carrying that symbol. If the data changes, regenerate and review the appropriate file rather than editing the human-readable text alone.

The artwork handoff checklist handles the wider file package. This sheet adds a specific source-to-symbol chain so the data decision remains visible.

Use a source-data validation sheet

Keep one row per symbol and packaging use. The prompts below contain no real identifier and are not production barcode data.

Checkpoint Record Responsible confirmation
Source Product identity, exact data and version Brand data owner
Use Retail unit, logistics or other named purpose Relevant channel or barcode specialist
Generated asset File, generation settings and date Responsible generating service
Decoded content Actual read result compared with source Agreed data validation reviewer
Artwork File revision and symbol location Artwork owner
Printed quality Proposed sample and verification scope Printer and qualified reviewer

Keep open cells visible. A symbol placed correctly in the design does not close the data-owner or printed-quality rows.

Follow a hypothetical two-product handoff

Suppose a gift brand has two similar ornament variants. The designer receives two approved source records and two generated assets. Their product names look similar, so the handoff sheet ties each asset to its exact variant before placement.

The artwork reviewer compares the decoded content with the corresponding source and records which symbol belongs to which file. If one asset was copied to both layouts, the mismatch becomes a located correction rather than a general request to check barcodes.

After correction, the printer still needs to review placement, reproduction and the relevant quality requirements on the proposed packaging. A scan from a screen image closes neither that physical review nor the channel’s acceptance requirements.

Keep a mismatch attached to the affected variant

In the hypothetical ornament handoff, call the variants V-A and V-B rather than using near-identical descriptive filenames alone. Each has its own approved source record, generated asset and artwork revision. Keep a mismatch on the affected variant row until the responsible owner confirms the corrected chain.

A decoded value that differs from the source should be recorded exactly in the private project record by the authorized reviewer. This public worksheet doesn’t need customer identifiers or real sample data. The correction request can name the variant and file versions without publishing those values.

Ask the data owner: ‘Please confirm the current source for V-B and identify which generated asset belongs in artwork A-B2.’ The designer should then update the asset, not merely the readable text beside an unchanged symbol.

After correction, keep data validation and physical verification as separate statuses. The first may be documented while the printer’s sample review remains pending. If the symbol type, placement or printing changes, ask the relevant specialist which review must be repeated. That preserves the chain without presenting a successful screen decode as a quality certificate.

Keep validation and verification separate

Data validation asks whether the encoded content matches the intended source. Printed-symbol verification asks a different quality question under the relevant method. Record the scope and responsible reviewer for each without using a casual phone scan as certification.

Send the source chain and unresolved artwork or print questions through Packrivo’s enquiry. The brand or its barcode specialist must confirm the data and applicable requirements; packaging coordination can keep those confirmations connected to the correct revision.

Separate the use scope before carrying a source change into artwork

Extend the fictional two-ornament example with two named use scopes: RETAIL and INFO. In this exercise the data owner keeps separate proposed asset records for each variant/use combination. That is not a rule requiring two symbols on a pack: a qualified owner may confirm that one actual asset serves multiple uses, in which case the map should reuse that exact reference rather than invent another.

A_RETAIL A_RETAIL uses generated GEN-A-R
A_RETAIL A_RETAIL uses artwork ART-A-R
A_INFO A_INFO uses source SRC-A-I
A_INFO A_INFO uses generated GEN-A-I
A_INFO A_INFO uses artwork ART-A-I
B_RETAIL B_RETAIL uses source SRC-B-R
B_RETAIL B_RETAIL uses generated GEN-B-R
B_RETAIL B_RETAIL uses artwork ART-B-R

B_INFO B_INFO uses generated GEN-B-I-r2
B_INFO B_INFO uses artwork ART-B-I-r2

The new map has A_RETAIL, A_INFO, B_RETAIL and B_INFO chains. Assume the owner revises only B_INFO's source reference to SRC-B-I-r2. Its corresponding generated and artwork references become GEN-B-I-r2 and ART-B-I-r2. The other three reference chains remain recorded under their own scope. This invented source change is not a decision about assigning a real identifier, changing a GTIN or satisfying any retail channel.

Ask which generated file actually follows the revised source and which output carries it. A designer changing readable words beside an unchanged asset leaves that question open. Compare the generated content with the correct approved source through the agreed method, preserving exact strings and leading characters in the private authorized record. The public CSV contains only reference tokens; it supplies no actual payload, URL, identifier or scannable symbol. The CSV has separate blank exact-data and exact-decoded-string fields. Each of the four records has separate decoded-data and printed-quality requests. A confirmed source chain for B_INFO does not close B_RETAIL or any physical print review. If symbol type, print process or position also changes, identify that scope for the relevant specialist. The buyer's useful output is the precise affected chain, retained references and missing evidence, rather than a general statement that the barcodes were checked.

title: Received Label Rolls Need Condition and Identity Checks Before Application
html:
Check received label rolls against their expected identity and visible condition before application begins. Record the roll, lot, artwork and web references, then locate any core, edge, liner or face issue. Keep the release decision with a named owner; visual receipt checks do not establish the final applied bond.

Identify the roll before inspecting its condition

The original UPM liner explanation describes the backing that carries and protects the adhesive through converting and application. This helps separate liner condition from label-face appearance. It is not a general receipt-inspection or release standard.

Match the delivery identification to the expected label configuration. Record the artwork revision, roll/lot identity and available supplier web drawing. Check which fields are present and which remain unknown before the roll is taken to the intended application area.

Preserve the roll label and any actual splice information supplied with it. A matching artwork name alone does not establish that the liner, adhesive or web arrangement is the expected proposal. Ask the converter to identify those components when the receipt record leaves them unclear.

Locate visible issues at the roll and web

The L200A label/web manual identifies equipment-specific web and dispensing conditions. Use the selected machine’s actual applicable reference for the application question, with a qualified owner confirming it. A visual receipt photograph is a different evidence type.

Inspect and record the visible core, roll edges, liner and label faces using the project’s agreed receipt method. Describe a crushed core, damaged edge, unclear identification or another actual observation at its location. Keep the packaging condition and photographs with the roll ID.

Where a visible issue or identity mismatch requires review, record the affected quantity or range if known. Keep an uncertain range explicitly open and assign the next owner. Avoid diagnosing the cause from a receipt image or releasing the roll because only its printed face appears correct.

Use a label-roll receipt register

The next converter response should identify the offered construction rather than asking the buyer to infer it from the color of the backing.

If a visible edge condition also needs review, keep it attached to that roll. The application owner can decide what further inspection or trial is required under the actual equipment plan, while the buyer retains the disposition and its evidence. A later successful label application should be recorded as another observation, not used to rewrite the receipt record.

Keep receipt, dispensing and adhesion evidence separate

The roll-or-sheet guide records the intended application arrangement. Use the adhesion and surface-condition method when the label is assessed on the actual product. The acceptance record provides the project requirement/evidence/decision structure.

The receiver records roll identities and visible condition. The converter confirms the offered construction. The qualified application owner addresses machine-specific questions, and the named decision owner resolves the roll’s use status. Keep the evidence for each role visible.

title: Label Liner Release vs Adhesion: Review Both Interfaces
html:
Review liner release through the intended hand or applicator route before treating the final surface bond as accepted. Record the label face, adhesive and liner identities plus the actual dispensing observation. Release from the backing and adhesion on the product are different interfaces that need separate evidence.

Identify the liner’s role before peeling

The original UPM liner explanation describes the liner as protecting the adhesive and carrying the label through converting and application. That supports recording the liner alongside the face and adhesive rather than identifying a label only by its visible paper or film.

Ask the converter for the offered face/adhesive/liner construction and drawing reference. State whether labels will be applied by hand, through a selected applicator or through another confirmed route. The peel or dispensing path is an input to the review, not a universal property of every liner.

Keep the actual target surface and product state identified too, but retain its applied-bond result separately. A label leaving its liner clearly does not by itself answer the subsequent adhesion question.

Record dispensing under the intended route

The Primera AP550 manual identifies its label/roll and sensing requirements. Where an applicator is selected, its qualified operator should confirm the applicable instructions and setup. This article gives a decision record, not machine calibration or repair directions.

Use the agreed label construction and application route for the observation. Record a label remaining on the liner, an observed edge problem, liner damage or another visible dispensing issue by its location and conditions. Ask the converter and application owner to assess that specific evidence.

If the proposal changes the liner or adhesive, retain the old construction and the revised identities. A response saying that the label is easier to peel should still identify the actual proposed component and evidence. Keep the later applied-surface test at its own sample reference.

Use a release and application-route log

This original Packrivo aid separates the two interfaces in a hypothetical candle-label plan.

Interface or field Example input Next evidence or owner

Release route Selected hand or applicator path Packing owner records actual route
Machine reference Applicable model/specification if used Qualified operator confirms requirements

Applied surface Finished candle container in named conditions Keep a separate applied-label sample
Revised proposal Changed liner/adhesive identity if offered Retain earlier result and next review owner

Compare an illustrative release question

Imagine the artwork and visible label face are approved, but the packing owner records a dispensing problem. Start with the offered construction and actual release route. The converter’s next answer should address those identities rather than recommending a stronger final adhesive without explaining the dispensing question.

If a revised liner is proposed, compare the release evidence using the intended route. Then carry the revised construction into the separate applied-surface review. This keeps an improvement at one interface from being mistaken for approval of the whole label system.

Handoff release and adhesion as linked records

Use the label adhesion and surface-condition method for the applied product surface. The roll-or-sheet guide records the broader application arrangement, while the sample revision record keeps a changed construction visible.

The converter confirms layer identities. The application owner reports the actual release observation. The buyer retains separate dispensing and applied-bond decisions with the evidence they use. If a field remains unresolved, keep its next owner and required response explicit.

Bring the face/adhesive/liner map and actual release question through your packaging brief. MOQ is 500 pieces per design; label construction, samples and commercial details are confirmed for the project.

title: Wrap Label Overlaps: Locate the Joint Before Artwork
html:
Locate the start edge and overlap of a wrap label on the actual container before approving artwork. Mark which copy becomes hidden and which edge finishes outside. Review the applied sample in its intended front view, with the same application direction used in the brief.

A flat label file shows all artwork at once. The customer sees it around a container, with one edge covering another if overlap is proposed. Give that join a location before the artwork becomes fixed.

Choose a front and an application direction

Identify the container’s intended front using a physical feature or a working reference mark. State how the container will stand during application. If it has no fixed front, choose the presentation view you want to review.

Avery’s label application guidance discusses alignment against a container seam or a straight reference. Use that principle to name your application reference. Its instructions do not define the overlap for your proposed label.

Mark the label’s starting edge and the direction it travels around the container. Identify the edge that will finish on top. Keep that direction with the artwork file; reversing it can hide a different portion of copy.

The label surface and use guide addresses the wider material proposal. This map focuses on the seam and artwork visibility after wrapping.

Separate overlap geometry from hidden content

Ask the supplier to confirm the proposed label length and overlap on the actual container geometry. Keep the container revision and label revision together. A nominal diameter alone may leave the application position or shape unclear.

Show the proposed covered area on a copy of the flat artwork. Mark any instruction, design feature or data that falls there. Avoid treating a hidden segment as still available to the customer simply because it exists in the file.

Keep required information outside an unresolved covered area until the responsible artwork owner confirms its placement. If a data carrier is involved, follow its relevant implementation requirements rather than squeezing it into the join by eye.

Record the desired seam view. It may be a rear presentation face, but that choice should come from actual handling and display, not an automatic rule that every seam belongs at the back.

Use a seam and hidden-copy map

Make a flat strip sketch and a formed container sketch with matching reference points. Add the following record beside them.

Field Flat label Applied sample
Start edge Named edge and artwork reference Position against container front
Travel direction Direction across flat strip Actual wrap direction
Outside edge Edge that finishes on top Seam location and visible edge
Covered area Copy or motif under overlap Actual hidden content
Reference Label and container revisions Matched sample and application note

If application direction is undecided, show both proposals separately. Do not blend their favourable views into one apparent approved layout.

Follow a hypothetical round gift container

Suppose a brand uses a wrap label around a round gift tin. The main motif is on the front, while a small care line sits near one end of the flat strip. The proposed overlap could cover the end of that line.

The buyer marks the starting edge, travel direction and covered region before asking the supplier to review length and application. The artwork owner then moves the care line to an available area if that proposal is confirmed.

The applied sample is viewed from the intended front and from the seam side. The record notes the actual covered copy and edge position. It does not infer adhesive suitability or long-term performance from a neat overlap.

Preserve the hidden-copy check after length changes

For the hypothetical tin label, identify the starting edge E1 and the final outside edge E2. Give the care line a separate artwork ID. The seam map then shows which portion of that line would sit under E2 in the proposed wrap direction.

If the label length changes, revisit the covered region before sending the file. A designer who shortens a blank-looking end can still alter seam position or the area hidden after application. Keep the original and revised strip maps rather than replacing one without a record.

Ask the supplier: ‘Please confirm the applied overlap and E2 position against the marked container front for label revision L2.’ That makes the sample question specific. A flat label proof answers the artwork layout but leaves the applied position open.

After the sample is applied, compare the visible copy with the same map. Record any different application direction as a changed condition. If the intended method is confirmed, carry that direction into the instruction and artwork handoff together. The useful result is an applied reference that the next operator can reproduce, without implying the overlap demonstrates adhesive suitability.

Give the artwork owner a formed reference

Send the strip map, container front, application direction and supplier overlap response through the packaging enquiry. Approve the artwork against the applied configuration. Keep the seam map available for later revisions so a length or direction change reopens the hidden-copy check.

Keep both wrapping directions through a label-length revision

Use two hypothetical application directions around the same FRONT1 reference. DIR_A starts at E1 and leaves E2 outside; DIR_B starts at E2 and leaves E1 outside. Neither direction nor any overlap dimension is approved.

The applied front and seam-side views are still needed; do not combine the better view from each direction into one apparent approved arrangement. title: Record Removal Conditions Before Asking for a Removable Label
html:
Before requesting a removable label, record the actual receiving surface, intended time in place and removal action. Review residue, label condition and surface appearance separately on an identified sample. A label described as removable still needs confirmation for the proposed surface and use conditions.

This method begins with the end of the label’s job. Decide what the customer or staff member should do when removing it, then ask the supplier to propose an identified construction for that use.

Describe the surface and removal purpose

Avery’s adhesive comparison distinguishes removable and repositionable categories and identifies surface-related limitations in its own products. That supports asking a specific use question, not assuming every removable label performs alike.

Record the actual finished receiving surface, including coating or wrap where relevant. A label on bare glass and one on a printed paper lid have different review inputs. Keep them in separate records even when the artwork is identical.

State why the label is removed. A temporary price sticker, closure label and reusable-container identifier can have different expectations for label condition and surface appearance after removal.

The label adhesion guide covers application and use. This sheet adds a narrower end-state record for removal instead of repeating that wider brief.

Agree the time and action to review

Provide the expected time between application and removal. If the range is broad, name the different review conditions with the supplier. Avoid selecting a convenient short trial and treating it as evidence for a much longer use.

Ask the supplier for instructions suited to the candidate label and actual surface. Do not improvise solvents, heat or sharp tools as a general removal recommendation. If the intended customer action is hand peeling, state that requirement clearly.

Record application conditions as context, but keep the removal questions separate. An application problem and residue after a later removal are different observations. The supplier needs both if they occur.

Use a removal condition and result sheet

Make one record for each candidate and use condition. Photograph the surface before applying the label where practical.

Field Condition to record Result to keep
Receiving surface Material, finish and component revision Starting surface image
Label identity Candidate construction and sample ID Supplier reference
Time in place Application and removal dates or agreed interval Actual recorded interval
Removal action Supplier instruction and intended user Action performed and any deviation
Residue Named location and viewing condition Visible residue, none observed or uncertain
Surface and label Separate post-removal views Visible surface change and label condition

Use ‘none observed under this view’ when that is the evidence. It is more accurate than converting a visual check into a guarantee of residue-free removal in all conditions.

Follow a hypothetical gift-lid sticker

Suppose a brand wants a temporary price sticker on a wrapped gift lid. The customer is expected to peel it by hand after purchase. The buyer records the actual lid wrap, candidate label and intended interval before asking for a sample proposal.

At the agreed review point, the sticker is removed using the confirmed instruction. The record keeps residue and lid appearance in different cells. A clean-looking lid with a torn label answers the surface question differently from the label-reuse question.

If the brand also wants the label reapplied elsewhere, add that as a new use requirement. It should not be assumed from the word ‘removable’. Ask for a candidate and evidence that address the extra action.

When a revised label or wrap is proposed, repeat the relevant condition record. Carrying approval from an earlier material would leave the actual receiving surface unreviewed.

State the post-removal result you need

For the hypothetical price sticker, the brand can require the lid to remain presentable after the intended hand-peel action while allowing the discarded label to tear. A request to reuse the label would add another requirement. Put both end-state choices into different fields so the supplier does not have to infer them.

Call the receiving lid surface R1 and the candidate label L1. Record the actual interval and the instruction followed at removal. If the label is removed earlier than planned, mark the result as covering that shorter condition rather than the full intended use.

A useful question is: ‘Please propose a label for R1 under the stated interval and hand-removal action, and confirm the review instructions.’ It connects the candidate to the actual surface and use. A generic removable-label name leaves those conditions unresolved.

Keep residue and surface appearance in separate post-removal views. A light change in the printed surface may need a different discussion from visible adhesive residue. Record what can be seen without assigning a cause. The next review should name the condition and candidate revision rather than repeat an unsupported claim of clean removal.

Send the end-state requirement

Bring the sheet, surface reference and intended removal action to Packrivo’s enquiry. Ask for a proposal and review scope tied to those conditions. Keep any unconfirmed removal interval or surface construction visible until the responsible supplier responds.

Reapplication adds a second receiving-surface decision

Keep the original price-sticker example's end state explicit. DISCARD21 requests removal from wrapped lid R1 while allowing the discarded label to tear if that is the actual agreed requirement. REUSE21 adds another request: the removed L1, with offered adhesive A1, is proposed for a second receiving surface R2. Neither route has an actual result, and R2's material and finish are deliberately unspecified.

Hypothetical configuration Named object Relationship Input or next scope
REUSE21 L1_A1 proposed reapplication to R2

Both routes still need R1 residue, R1 surface appearance and removed-label condition recorded separately. Reuse then adds the L1/A1-to-R2 reapplication relationship. A presentable first lid does not show that the removed label can be read, handled or bonded at the second destination. A label remaining intact is not evidence of the new surface bond either. Ask for a candidate and instructions addressing that complete use rather than transferring a removable category name into a repositioning claim.

Retain the actual time in place and supplier-confirmed hand-removal instruction. An early removal covers its shorter condition, not the longer intended interval. If the wrap, receiving finish, adhesive or method changes, create another condition record. The original bare-glass and printed-paper examples remain separate surface choices; identical artwork is not a reason to combine their removal evidence.

The worksheet leaves actual interval, surface construction, method, observations, decisions and evidence empty. It contains no solvent, heat or tool recommendation and no default residue-free claim. The buyer can decide whether a discard-only requirement is enough or whether the extra reuse scope is worth requesting. Any acceptance must identify the actual label, adhesive, receiving surfaces and conditions it covers.

ACTUAL_BLANK is a separate empty starting row; enter permitted project evidence before using an actual record. A blank means unknown.

Use the Label Adhesion for Packaging Needs Surface and Use Details for its separate question. Use the Liner Release and Final Label Adhesion Need Separate Review Records for its separate question.

title: Label Liner Width, Gap and Pitch for the Applicator
html:
Specify label width, liner width and gap or pitch against the same selected applicator reference. Keep the converter’s roll drawing and the machine owner’s confirmation together before ordering. These dimensions describe different parts of the web, so a label’s visible size alone cannot close the application brief.

A Rectangle roll labels is a format reference, not an applicator specification. Send the actual label outline, liner width, gap or pitch and machine-owner requirements together before confirming the supplied roll.

Name the label and web dimensions separately

The original L200A label/web specification distinguishes machine-related label and backing requirements. The Primera AP550 manual also has label/roll specifications and sensor-related fields. Each source applies to its named machine, not to every label applicator.

Record the selected model, applicable manual/specification version and application route. Give the converter that reference before asking for a roll proposal. If no machine has been selected, keep compatibility open rather than presenting a generic gap as an accepted requirement.

Label the width of the face label, the width of the backing liner and the gap or pitch in the feed direction on one web drawing. Include the edge margins and actual sensing method if supplied by the machine owner. Units and measurement direction should remain visible beside each field.

Compare one web proposal with one machine reference

Ask the converter to return the proposed web layout and the relevant material identities. Ask the qualified machine owner to confirm which dimensions and sensing fields apply to the intended setup. The buyer should receive their responses about the same drawing revision.

If the machine reference and offered layout conflict, locate the exact field. A wider liner, changed gap or different sensor proposal can alter another part of the web. Record the changed scope and obtain a revised drawing or trial plan instead of accepting an isolated dimension by email.

Keep manual or machine-assisted application routes separate. A label that can be peeled by hand still needs its own equipment compatibility review when the plan changes to an applicator.

Use an applicator web-dimension table

This original Packrivo aid leaves numerical requirements to the actual machine reference.

Field Hypothetical handoff entry Who completes it
Machine reference Selected model M1 and applicable manual Equipment owner supplies the reference
Label width/length Face label outline on drawing LP1 Converter supplies proposed dimensions and units
Liner width Backing edges shown separately from label Converter identifies margin/layout proposal
Gap or pitch Feed-direction field G1 on LP1 Machine owner confirms applicable requirement
Sensing Actual sensing method and material question Qualified operator/converter confirms compatibility
Decision Accept layout or request specific revision/trial Buyer retains both responses and next owner

Review a hypothetical roll response

Imagine a supplier confirms the printed label width but leaves the liner width and gap unspecified. The application question remains open even if the artwork is ready. Request the complete web drawing and the selected machine’s applicable fields.

If another supplier uses a different gap or liner, keep those as separate proposals. Compare their equipment responses before deciding the application arrangement. The useful result is a confirmed layout or a named compatibility question, not a table where every missing dimension is filled with an assumed industry default.

Send the web drawing with the application owner

The roll-or-sheet guide sets the broader format choice. Use the adhesion and surface-condition article for the separate question of how the applied label meets the actual product surface.

The equipment owner provides the applicable reference. The converter provides the offered web. The qualified operator confirms the intended setup, while the buyer retains the selected configuration and next trial question. No packing method or machine adjustment is authorized merely by this planning table.

Bring the web layout, selected reference and unresolved dimension/sensing fields to your packaging brief. MOQ is 500 pieces per design; the actual label proposal, sample scope and commercial conditions are confirmed for the project.

Check width and feed arithmetic before asking about the machine

For invented web LP1, assume liner width 54 mm, face-label width 50 mm, and side margins 2 mm each. Along feed, assume label height 30 mm and gap 3 mm, giving pitch 33 mm. These are illustrative geometry inputs, not settings for AP550, L200A or another machine.

Direction Input Arithmetic Still unresolved
Across web 50 mm label;2 mm each margin 2 + 50 + 2 =54 mm liner Machine width and layout acceptance
Along feed 30 mm label height;3 mm gap 30 +3 =33 mm pitch Applicable machine/sensor requirements
Sensing Not selected No default assumed Material and actual sensing method
Trial Not performed No rate calculated Actual proposed setup

Pitch here means the same leading-edge point on one label to the same point on the next; it includes one label height and one gap. It is not merely the gap. The final diagram shows two complete face labels, with numeric width and feed directions kept separate.

Record the selected machine and applicable manual before ordering stock. The CSV leaves that reference, sensing and compatibility decision blank. Even correct arithmetic does not show whether a stock/liner works with a particular sensor or peel edge. These values must not be adopted as a universal gap or copied into an AP550/L200A stock order; their owner must confirm the actual requirements and proposal.

Download the label liner width gap and pitch record (.csv). HYPOTHETICAL rows are invented examples. Use ACTUAL_BLANK for permitted project inputs; replace that row label only when recording actual facts. Empty evidence, observation and date fields mean unknown or not performed, never acceptance. Keep checkpoints and revisions separate.

Send the complete web drawing and actual machine/manual/sensing references before requesting a confirmed layout or trial. Packrivo coordinates independent suppliers. These records establish no supplier offer, service availability or MOQ exception; its published baseline is 500 pieces per product/design.

title: Label Roll Changeovers Need Splice Identification Before Application
html:
Give every label-roll changeover an outgoing roll ID, incoming roll ID and any known splice marker or affected-label range. Keep the applicator’s actual requirements with that event. This preserves an answerable handoff when a roll changes, without repeating the earlier core and winding-direction selection.

Separate the roll specification from the change event

The original Shibuya Hoppmann L200A manual includes label/web and splice conditions for that machine. It demonstrates that splice compatibility is equipment-specific. The actual operator and converter should use the selected machine’s applicable instructions; this worksheet does not prescribe machine setup or repair.

The existing roll-or-sheet label guide helps select the application and roll format. A changeover event adds a different record: which roll leaves, which roll enters and how any splice or uncertain label section is identified.

Record the roll and lot labels provided with the delivery, the artwork/configuration revision and the intended applicator. Keep missing information explicit. If the roll contains a marked splice or the supplier states a splice condition, attach that actual description rather than guessing where it occurs.

Preserve the affected range without diagnosing the machine

Ask the packing owner to name the event and the observation that prompted it. The event may be an ordinary roll replacement or a question about a marked splice. Record which labels or units are affected if that information is known, and say when the range is still uncertain.

Use the project’s agreed status and owner for labels awaiting review. The qualified operator handles the machine-related confirmation, while the label converter confirms the offered web/splice construction. A supervisor or buyer decides what further evidence is needed for the affected packout.

Retain the previous roll identity and its event record when the new roll begins. Overwriting the old ID with the new one loses the link between an observation and the labels that were actually used.

Use a roll-change and splice-event table

This original Packrivo record uses hypothetical rolls, not actual production or customer data.

Incoming roll Roll R2, expected same configuration Check supplier identification before use

Resolve a hypothetical unclear changeover

Imagine a new roll enters while the earlier roll has a marked splice question. Keep R1’s observation linked to R1, even if R2 appears to apply normally. The next response should identify the splice condition and affected range rather than simply saying the new roll is working.

If the range cannot be established, retain that uncertainty and ask the responsible packing owner what trace information is available. The buyer can then decide which evidence or additional review is required, without treating a new roll as proof that every earlier unit is acceptable.

Handoff the event with the correct owner

Use the label adhesion and surface-condition method for the separate applied-label question. The acceptance record keeps requirement, evidence and disposition visible when the affected units need review.

The converter supplies roll/web facts. The qualified operator confirms the selected machine requirements. The packing owner records the event and affected items, and the named project decision owner resolves their status. Keep these responsibilities in the record rather than inserting generic operational instructions.

Share the roll IDs, actual splice description and unresolved event fields through your packaging brief. MOQ is 500 pieces per design; the label construction, sample scope and commercial conditions are confirmed for the project.

These ten references demonstrate a source map, not ten production scenarios, a real delivery, an inspection sample or a measured application result. Request the converter's actual splice identification and the packing owner's trace information for R1. A statement that R2 appears to apply normally does not release R1's earlier scope. The CSV therefore retains separate affected-scope and own-use rows for each roll alongside the event, artwork and SP1 relationships.

This is a traceability example, not a machine instruction. Core, winding and web requirements remain with the selected applicator's qualified owner and actual manual. title: Exposed Board Edges Need a Separate Color Decision After Converting
html:
Give exposed cut and turned board edges their own color decision beside the adjacent finished face. Identify the actual core, wrap or substrate visible at each edge, then review the converted sample under the agreed conditions. This keeps an edge-color choice separate from general face-color approval.

Name the exposed edge and the neighboring face

This is an original Packrivo observation map. Its evidence comes from the actual offered material identity and converted sample; it does not claim a universal board-color or edge-performance rule.

Mark each relevant cut edge or turned wrapping edge on the current component drawing. Identify the adjacent printed or finished face and the material layer exposed at that location. A colored front face and a visible substrate edge may need different appearance decisions.

Ask the converter to identify the offered board/core and wrap construction. Keep a grade or surface description with the sample rather than assuming that a screen color or an outside finish identifies the inside substrate.

Review the actual converted state

Inspect the named edge beside its finished face after cutting, wrapping or the relevant converting operation. Record the sample revision, orientation and viewing conditions. Use a close-up to locate the edge and a wider view to show how it appears on the component.

The buyer can retain the visible edge color, request another material/edge proposal or keep the question open. Record which option is chosen and the evidence it uses. Avoid silently accepting an edge because the main face color has already been approved.

If another proposal changes the wrap, core or exposed boundary, keep those differences visible. Compare the same edge/face relationship on the new sample so a relocated opening does not hide a changed material appearance.

Use an exposed-edge color map

The hypothetical rigid-window lid below uses illustrative references, not an actual customer sample.

Edge/face relationship Example record Decision or next evidence
Cut edge E1 Core visible beside viewing aperture A1 Converter identifies actual material layer
Turned edge E2 Wrapping edge beside the same opening Record finished wrap proposal
Adjacent face F1 Accepted printed/finished face reference Retain reference and conditions
Converted sample Lid sample S1, drawing L1_r02 Edge close-up and complete component view
Observation Visible edge color beside F1 Buyer records actual appearance observation
Disposition Retain, change or review named edge Named owner and next sample/reference

Resolve an illustrative window-edge question

Imagine the finished face of a rigid lid matches the buyer’s reference, while its cut aperture shows a different substrate color. Keep the two appearance fields separate. Ask the converter for the material/edge identity and the proposed treatment or material option before deciding what should change.

The buyer may prefer the exposed edge as a deliberate visual detail. Alternatively, another proposed wrap/core arrangement may need a new sample. In both cases the decision should name E1 and the accepted configuration rather than being folded into a general statement that the lid color is approved.

Handoff the edge decision with its drawing

Use the physical color approval method for the reference and viewing conditions. The drawing-change record keeps a moved aperture or edge linked to the artwork and holder checks. The window-lid rigid gift box is a relevant construction comparison for core/wrap/patch interfaces.

The converter identifies the actual exposed layer. The observer returns the converted edge/face evidence, and the buyer decides the appearance or asks for a specific new proposal. Keep that decision with the same drawing and sample revision.

Bring the edge map, adjacent-face reference and unresolved material/appearance fields to your packaging brief. MOQ is 500 pieces per design; materials, samples and commercial terms are confirmed for the project.

Check core and wrap alternatives without carrying face approval onto the edges

For the hypothetical window lid, keep aperture A1, adjacent face F1, cut edge E1 and turned edge E2 fixed as references. Compare BASE21 using B1 core and W1 wrap with CORE_CHANGE21 using B2/W1 and WRAP_CHANGE21 using B1/W2. These are material identities for a proposal, not observed colors or assumptions that a wrap hides an edge.

Hypothetical configuration Named object Relationship Input or next scope

BASE21 BASE21 uses wrap W1
CORE_CHANGE21 CORE_CHANGE21 uses core B2
CORE_CHANGE21 CORE_CHANGE21 uses wrap W1
WRAP_CHANGE21 WRAP_CHANGE21 uses core B1
WRAP_CHANGE21 WRAP_CHANGE21 uses wrap W2

Review F1, E1 and E2 independently on each converted candidate. A core change may alter what is exposed at E1 while the same wrap remains. A wrap change can affect E2 and the face appearance even though the underlying core identity is retained. Ask the converter which layer is actually visible at each boundary before deciding what the photograph represents.

The original fictional face-color acceptance covers F1 only. It does not preselect retaining E1 or E2. The buyer may deliberately retain a contrasting exposed edge, request a different material or edge proposal, or keep the question open. Preserve the actual reference and viewing conditions with whichever scoped decision is eventually made. Screen hues in a diagram are not those physical references.

If the aperture itself moves, give the changed geometry a new drawing relationship rather than comparing unrelated edges under the same A1 label. The worksheet retains sample S1 and original drawing L1_r02 as baseline identities, then adds candidate-specific material and three-surface requests. No edge color, cover-up treatment, acceptable difference or universal board property is supplied. The useful next response identifies the exposed construction and returns converted evidence for the named edge and adjacent face.

title: Describe Surface Scuffs Before Requesting a Finish Change
html:
Describe a packaging scuff by the named surface, location and action that preceded it before requesting a different finish. Keep a before view, an after view and the sample revision together. A visible mark is an observation; it doesn’t establish the cause or prove that a proposed coating will solve it.

A request for ‘anti-scuff packaging’ can skip the useful information. The supplier needs to know where the mark appeared, what that surface is and how it was handled. Start with a located record instead of a treatment name.

Name the surface that carries the mark

Record the component and face, such as the sleeve’s inside rear seam area or the lid’s outside front panel. Include the proposed substrate, print and finish if known. If the surface construction is unclear, make that the first question.

Holmen’s technical information treats surface roughness and surface strength as separate properties. That distinction supports keeping a buyer’s visible scuff observation separate from material-sheet properties or technical test results.

Use a simple map with a location ID. A wide photograph should show where that ID sits on the component. A close-up alone can be hard to relate to the drawing.

The print finish brief is useful when a treatment is being proposed. This record comes before that choice, so the proposed change has a defined problem to address.

Record the action before the mark

Describe what happened to the sample before the mark was noticed. Examples include sliding a loaded tray, stacking two empty lids or moving the pack on a counter. Keep the words factual and avoid diagnosing friction, pressure or abrasion without evidence.

State whether the surface already had a mark in the starting view. If there is no starting photograph, record ‘starting condition not documented’. That gap matters because the after view cannot show when the mark appeared.

Keep repeated actions within a named review scope. Don’t invent a number of rubs or an improvised pass rule and present it as a standard. If a repeatable test is needed, ask the responsible party to agree its method and acceptance criteria.

Use a named-surface observation form

Make one record for one sample and one location. Use separate rows or records for different faces.

Field Entry to record Evidence
Location Component, face and marked area ID Wide and close views
Surface Substrate, print and proposed finish Supplier description or unresolved question
Starting state Visible condition before action Before photo or declared gap
Action history Named handling step and contents Short sequence description
Observed mark Position, shape and viewing condition After photo under stated light
Next response Cause assessment or candidate revision Supplier reply linked to record

Separate a mark on an outside panel from a mark at a moving seam. They may call for different construction or handling questions even if the same green artwork makes them look similar.

Work through a hypothetical sleeve mark

Suppose a brand reviews a loaded tray in a printed sleeve. After removal, the reviewer notices a pale mark on the sleeve near its internal seam. The starting condition was photographed, and the mark wasn’t visible in that view.

The buyer records the tray and sleeve revisions, loaded contents and the single removal action used. A contact map identifies the seam location. The supplier is asked to review that interface before a new exterior finish is requested.

If a candidate revision changes the seam position, record that as a construction change. If it changes the surface treatment, record that instead. A later comparison should use the same action and contents so the observation remains useful.

A revised sample with no visible mark under the stated view can close that observation scope. It doesn’t prove unlimited wear resistance or protection across every handling condition.

Separate a located mark from a candidate treatment

For the hypothetical sleeve observation, call the seam-side mark M1 and keep the preceding tray action A1. The material field identifies the proposed surface; the cause field remains open. This gives a later candidate treatment a defined observation to address.

If the supplier proposes both a seam change and a finish change, record them as two different revision items. A revised sample can then be compared with A1 and the same contents. An attractive outside image alone does not tell the buyer which interface was changed.

A precise request is: ‘Please assess M1 after A1 on sleeve S1 and state the candidate change and evidence needed.’ That invites a responsible review without instructing the supplier to add an unspecified coating. If the starting condition was not recorded, include that gap in the request.

Keep visual acceptance under stated conditions separate from any required repeatable test. If a technical evaluation becomes necessary, its agreed method and criteria should have their own record. The observation form can supply the location and action context without pretending it already measures abrasion resistance.

Give the supplier the located issue

Send the surface description, before-and-after views, action history and open question through Packrivo’s packaging enquiry. Ask for a response tied to the actual location. The next sample should identify what changed and what evidence is needed to review that change.

A combined seam and finish revision cannot isolate either change

Use the original fictional internal sleeve mark M1 after loaded-tray removal A1. Name the baseline S1/J1/V1. S2 proposes J2 while retaining V1; S3 retains J1 while proposing V2; S4 proposes both J2 and V2. The contents P1 and named A1 remain comparison inputs in all four configurations. No candidate has been observed to improve the mark.

Hypothetical configuration Named object Relationship Input or next scope
S1 S1 uses seam J1
S1 S1 uses finish V1
S2 S2 uses seam J2
S2 S2 uses finish V1
S3 S3 uses seam J1
S3 S3 uses finish V2
S4 S4 uses seam J2
S4 S4 uses finish V2

S2 requests evidence of the changed seam relationship under the same action. S3 requests evidence for the new surface proposal while the seam stays identified. S4 can be reviewed as a complete candidate, but its difference from S1 cannot by itself tell the buyer which changed field accounts for a visible result. If contents, grip or orientation changes too, record that new configuration before drawing even a limited comparison.

Keep the starting view's status independent of the revision. When M1 was not visible in the fictional starting photograph, that is a located appearance statement under that view. When the starting condition is undocumented, the time of mark appearance remains unresolved. An attractive after image cannot reconstruct it. The download keeps those evidence conditions separate rather than treating a missing before view as an absence of a mark.

The buyer's output is a comparison request naming the candidate, location, action and missing evidence. Actual before/after observations, methods and decisions remain blank. The original single removal action is not a rub-cycle standard, and a favorable appearance observation would not establish unlimited wear or transport protection. A required technical test needs its own agreed method and criteria; this record locates the question without prescribing a finish cure or test count.

title: Review Window Clarity With the Product Behind It
html:
Review a packaging window with the actual product and holder behind the proposed patch. Take a matched view with and without the patch where practical, and record angle, light and sample identity. Describe visibility and reflections as observations; a photograph doesn’t establish an optical grade or a universal clarity result.

This method starts after the opening position is broadly agreed. Its job is to make the window-view review repeatable enough to discuss. It should not turn a screen impression into a measured material specification.

Identify what the window sample represents

PakFactory’s window patching explanation distinguishes the film layer from the die-cut opening. Record the proposed patch material and supplier sample identity before comparing views. A different patch or a bare opening leaves a different question.

Ask whether the sample uses the proposed joining method and formed panel. If it is a loose material swatch, record that limitation. It can show one surface under one condition without representing a complete loaded window.

Choose the exact product face the customer should see. Keep the holder, product orientation and background fixed for the comparison. A repositioned product can make a window appear improved even though the patch is unchanged.

Plan a small set of matched views

Use a front view in the intended sales orientation and one relevant angled view. Add another only if the actual display or handling task needs it. Record the light source and camera position in plain words.

Where practical, compare the same arrangement without the patch and with the proposed patch. Keep the opening, product and viewpoint unchanged. If removing the patch changes the panel or holder, describe that limitation rather than pretending the pair isolates one variable.

Capture an overall pack view as well as a close-up. The overall view tells the reviewer whether the product is recognizable in the intended presentation. The close-up helps locate a reflection or obscured detail.

The sample approval checklist covers wider sample decisions. This photo plan deals specifically with the view through one proposed window.

Use a product-behind-window photo plan

Complete the plan before taking comparison photos. A photo file name should connect to a row and sample version.

View ID Condition Pair to capture Observation
V1 Front sales view, named light Without and with patch where practical Recognizable product face and covered areas
V2 Relevant side angle, same light Same product and holder position Reflections at identified locations
V3 if needed Actual handling or display condition Matched wider view Visibility during intended action
Sample reference Patch, panel and holder revisions Component identity image Final or substitute configuration
Decision Accepted view or open issue Specific photo IDs Next supplier question

Use a located description instead of a single clarity score. For example, record that the top of the ornament is covered by a reflection in V2 while the front view remains recognizable.

Work through a hypothetical reflective ornament

Suppose a carton window shows a polished ornament. In one angled photo, a bright reflection covers its decorative face. The buyer repeats the same product view without the patch where practical and records both images.

The pair helps frame a question about the window view under that condition. It doesn’t establish whether the reflection comes entirely from the patch, product surface or lighting. The supplier can review the named patch proposal and suggest useful further evidence.

If the buyer changes the holder position, record that as a new configuration. Keep the earlier patch comparison separate. The objective is to see which decision changed, not to collect only the most attractive photographs.

Keep the view plan separate from a photography choice

For the hypothetical polished ornament, call the straight customer view V1 and the relevant side view V2. Record the visible reflection in V2 without replacing it with a more attractive angle. A product photograph may be styled for publication, while this review image needs to preserve the agreed comparison condition.

If a matched bare-opening view cannot be obtained without disturbing the holder, write that limitation in the pair field. The supplier can suggest another sample or material reference. Don’t call the two images a controlled comparison when their product positions differ.

Ask the source: ‘Please review the patch proposal for the visibility issue in V2 with holder H1.’ That names the condition and component, while leaving the cause open. A reply changing the holder should create a new configuration row rather than overwrite the patch record.

The final decision may accept V1 and request another look at V2. Keep both scopes visible. A useful photo plan helps choose the next evidence for the actual display task; it does not require every possible light and angle, or turn ordinary photographs into a claim about laboratory clarity.

Keep the approval scope visible

A visual review can accept a presentation under stated conditions. A requirement for a measured optical property needs an appropriate specification and responsible evidence. Avoid assigning a laboratory term to an ordinary photograph.

Send the view plan, sample identities and located observations through the Packrivo enquiry. Ask the next question in terms of the actual view that remains unresolved, then review the relevant revised sample or evidence.

Start a new matched-pair group when the holder changes

A matched pair belongs to a complete configuration. In the fictional plan, H1 holds P21 with desired face PV1. Request V1-BARE and V1-PATCH from the same front view, then V2-BARE and V2-PATCH from the same relevant angled view. The four entries are planned photo requests, not captured evidence or four optical measurements.

Hypothetical configuration Named object Relationship Input or next scope
H1_V1_BARE H1_V1_BARE uses holder H1
H1_V1_BARE H1_V1_BARE uses patch state BARE
H1_V1_PATCH_P1 H1_V1_PATCH_P1 uses holder H1
H1_V1_PATCH_P1 H1_V1_PATCH_P1 uses patch state PATCH_P1
H1_V2_BARE H1_V2_BARE uses holder H1
H1_V2_BARE H1_V2_BARE uses patch state BARE
H1_V2_PATCH_P1 H1_V2_PATCH_P1 uses holder H1
H1_V2_PATCH_P1 H1_V2_PATCH_P1 uses patch state PATCH_P1
H2_V1_BARE H2_V1_BARE uses holder H2
H2_V1_BARE H2_V1_BARE uses patch state BARE

H2_V1_PATCH_P1 H2_V1_PATCH_P1 uses patch state PATCH_P1

If the supplier proposes H2, create a second group with its own four requests. H1's bare view should not be paired with H2's patched view to claim a patch contribution: the product arrangement changed too. Within either group, retain the same product orientation, background, light and viewpoint for the pair, then record any unavoidable difference. The CSV maps every request to product, face, holder, view and patch state.

A bare view is not always obtainable without disturbing the arrangement. Record whether it is practical, unavailable, or changes the holder/panel. Leave pair validity unresolved when the needed identities or conditions are missing; do not fill the absent member using a different product photograph. Ask the supplier what alternative sample or material evidence addresses the actual viewing question.

The original fictional V2 reflection and separate V1 recognition scope remain distinct. Neither identifies a cause or an optical grade. A buyer can accept one view and keep another open under its stated condition. Use wider and close views to locate the issue, while any measured transmission, haze or clarity requirement needs a suitable technical evidence basis. The teaching image contains only planned-view locators and empty evidence frames, without simulated better or worse film results.

title: Locate Window Patches Against the Product View
html:
Locate a window patch by separating the die-cut opening, the patch perimeter and the product view behind it. Confirm the attachment layout with the supplier and review the formed loaded pack. A window outline on artwork doesn’t show which areas are visible, joined or obscured by the contents.

The useful question is what the customer should see through the opening. Work backwards from that view, then ask how the proposed patch is attached. Keep the display intention and construction response distinct.

Draw three separate boundaries

PakFactory’s window packaging reference describes a film applied to a die-cut window. This supports distinguishing the opening from the patch. The actual film, joining area and construction need confirmation for the proposal.

On a working template, show the cut opening, proposed patch outline and the product’s projected view. Use separate layers or line styles. A single thick rectangle labelled ‘window’ leaves all three boundaries ambiguous.

Ask the supplier to confirm where the patch meets the panel and which joining regions must remain available. Do not draw a universal attachment width into the artwork without the proposed process details.

Use a fixed panel reference, such as the front face reading normally. Give the opening and patch positions against that reference rather than an unlabelled photograph that could be rotated.

Place the product in its actual holder

Show the sale-ready item and any card or insert behind the window. Record which product face should be visible. If the product can move within the proposed holder, state that as a fit question before relying on a precise view.

For a hypothetical ornament gift carton, the customer may need to see the ornament’s face rather than the holder’s blank edge. A side section helps show how the holder positions that face relative to the opening.

The insert fit guide addresses the product’s location. This template handles the relationship between that location and the window panel, rather than repeating the whole insert brief.

Use a window and attachment template

Keep the three boundaries aligned to the same panel and revision. The table adds the questions that a visual layout alone may miss.

Layer Information to show Confirmation
Cut opening Shape, position and current panel Supplier dieline revision
Patch perimeter Proposed patch outline beyond opening Material and construction proposal
Attachment Supplier-marked joining regions Process owner and confirmed scope
Product view Visible face with actual holder Loaded formed sample photo
Obstructions Card, rim, seam or other hidden area Located change request

A joining area can be outside the visible opening yet still interact with artwork or a fold. Keep that location in the construction response, not only in the product photo.

Follow a hypothetical view correction

Suppose the first layout centres a window on the carton panel. The product holder places the ornament higher than that opening. The buyer draws the actual view boundary and records that the desired face is partly hidden.

The team can then discuss moving the opening, changing the holder or changing the desired view. Those are separate options with different construction consequences. The template records which option the supplier proposes rather than enlarging the window by guesswork.

If the patch shape changes, ask whether the attachment proposal also changes. A revised visible opening does not automatically establish a revised joining layout. Keep both responses with the same dieline.

Use fixed references to compare a revised window

Give the hypothetical panel a fixed front reference and identify the product’s desired visible face as PV1. In the first proposal, PV1 is partly below the opening. Mark that relationship on the loaded view rather than describing the entire window as too small.

Ask the supplier to distinguish an opening-position revision from a holder-position revision. Both can alter the view, but they change different components. If the proposal changes both, preserve both revisions in the aligned template so the next sample is not mistaken for a window-only adjustment.

A useful response request is: ‘Please show PV1 against opening W1 and confirm the patch and attachment layout for the revised panel.’ It links the desired view to the construction. A larger cutout drawing with no patch outline leaves the joining question open.

Compare the next sample using the same product orientation and customer view. Record the patch revision, holder revision and actual visible boundary. If the desired view is accepted while the attachment remains provisional, retain separate statuses. The template should close exactly the relationship supported by the evidence rather than presenting the whole window assembly as confirmed.

Review the formed loaded pack

Inspect the intended view from the agreed customer angle. Photograph the wider front panel as well as the window close-up. Record any obscured area and the sample state, without claiming optical performance from a concept image.

Send the aligned template, complete product position and unresolved joining questions through Packrivo’s enquiry form. Approval should connect the window position to the supplier-confirmed construction and the loaded view, not merely to a flat artwork outline.

Keep the starting geometry fixed while choosing which component moves

The original narrative contains two positional descriptions: the holder places the ornament higher than an opening, and a separate PV1 example lies partly below an opening. Treat them as different hypothetical starting geometries, not one measurement to combine. The download assigns HIGHER_EXAMPLE and BELOW_EXAMPLE separately. An actual brief needs the located relationship under one fixed front reference. W_HIGH_CASE/H_HIGH_CASE and W_BELOW_CASE/H_BELOW_CASE are illustrative aliases, not actual revision histories. If real records describe the same configuration in opposite ways, retain that description conflict for clarification instead of presenting two valid measurements.

title: Glue Zones Need the Current Drawing and Surface Layers in One View
html:
Place the current glue zones, ink, coating and film layers on one drawing before closing the artwork handoff. Identify the actual bonding faces and the responsible converter, then retain any grade-specific compatibility question. Trim and bleed rules do not settle the glue interface.

Identify the joint and its bonding faces

Henkel’s folding-carton bonding explanation identifies the side seam as the bond that forms the carton tube. Use that context to ask the converter which joint and substrate faces are being bonded in the offered design.

Label the glue zone on the current blank and the receiving face it meets after folding. Include the joint preparation and assembly order. The zone should have a stable identity that appears in the artwork review and the formed-sample observation.

Map the ink, coating or film proposed on both faces of the joint. A design layer can occupy a bonding location even when it appears outside the customer-visible artwork. The converter and printer should see the same layer map when answering that question.

Use actual grade information for the conflict

The ACTEGA coating grade reference explicitly identifies one coating as non-glueable. That is a grade-specific example of why a joint needs its actual layer proposal. It is not a rule that all coatings or all inks behave identically at glue areas.

Ask the printer/finisher to name the offered layer and the converter to name the adhesive/process proposal. Request their response about the identified faces and any required exclusion or revision. Avoid filling an unknown area with a generic clearance value copied from another package.

If the response proposes removing a layer, moving a zone or changing an adhesive, record the exact field and drawing revision. Retain the earlier proposal so a later artwork update does not restore the unresolved conflict inadvertently.

title: Finish Contact Observations Need the Product Surface and Handling Conditions
html:
Record visible transfer or scuffing at a packaging-to-product contact point with the actual surface pair and handling conditions named. Keep the sample IDs, photographs and next action together. A visible mark is an observation to resolve; it does not establish a chemical migration result, a transport cause or a universal material performance.

Define both sides of the contact

The coating technical sheet identifies properties and application fields for a named coating grade. Use that reference to request the actual grade on your packaging surface rather than adopting its properties for every finished box.

A proposed holder may have a base, a surface layer and an exposed cut edge that need different identities. Ask the supplier to identify those construction interfaces on the offered holder, then record where they contact the product. The layer description does not prove how your product finish behaves.

Name the actual packaging face or edge and the product surface that touches it. Include primary wrapping or a liner if one sits between them. Record which finish, grade or layer is still a supplier proposal and which physical sample was actually reviewed.

Keep the handling sequence with the observation

Write the loading, closing, opening and removal actions used in the review. Identify where contact occurs during that sequence. A mark after removal should be linked to its observed location and conditions instead of being assigned a cause from the material name.

Retain views before handling, at the contact position and after the observation when available. State the lighting and any relevant known condition, and keep unknowns open. If the observer changes the grip, product orientation or packing arrangement, record the change before comparing another sample.

This tool concerns a packaging surface meeting the product. A record about two packaging faces rubbing against each other has a different contact pair and should remain separately identified. Keep that distinction visible when one gift contains several possible contact locations.

A new sample should repeat the agreed product and handling state so the buyer can compare the located contact. If the product finish or a protective primary wrap changes too, keep that difference visible. The comparison should show which interface was reviewed rather than promising scratch resistance from a material substitution.

title: Lamination and Varnish Need Separate Layers in the Packaging BOM
html:
Record lamination and varnish as different surface constructions in the packaging BOM. Identify each component face, film or coating grade, adhesive proposal and converting interface. A finish name should lead to a layer description that can be compared, sampled and revised without changing the rest of the pack silently.

Describe the layer on the named face

Holmen’s film-lamination explanation describes film joined to paperboard with adhesive, including thermal films with preapplied adhesive. This supports asking for the film and adhesive construction. It does not identify the grade offered for your particular box.

The coating technical reference separately identifies an applied UV coating, substrate recommendations and application fields for one grade. Use this distinction to keep a film laminate and an applied varnish/coating in separate proposal rows, even when both are described as gloss.

Name the component and face before recording the finish. A box exterior, lid interior, printed band and separate care card may have different layers. Include the base grade and printed surface underneath, so the proposal can be checked at the correct interface.

Keep adhesive and converting questions with the layer

Ask whether the offered film carries its own adhesive or uses a separately applied adhesive. Request the film/adhesive identities and the process scope relevant to that component. For a varnish or coating, request its actual grade and application proposal rather than assuming a visible sheen defines the construction.

Locate folds, cut edges, glue faces and any product-contact surface beside the layer. Ask the printer/converter to confirm which interfaces need a sample or another technical response. Keep grade-specific suitability and any required material-claim evidence separate from a generic finish preference.

When a supplier proposes changing from a film to a coating, record that as a layer-stack change. It may affect more than the appearance name. Retain the old and new proposals so the buyer can see which faces, processes and follow-up questions changed.

title: Spot-Gloss Masks Need a Named Panel and a Registered Boundary
html:
Give every spot-gloss mask a named panel, artwork revision and visible boundary. Map excluded fold and glue areas beside the intended gloss so the printer can confirm the actual coating and registration proposal. The buyer should review where the mask lands, not only how shiny the preview looks.

Keep the gloss mask separate from the printed artwork

The original coating-maker spot-varnish reference identifies a gloss UV overprint varnish and spot use under its specific conditions. Use it as a coating/process example. The selected printer still confirms the actual grade, application and mask alignment for your panel.

Name the gloss object and the panel it belongs to. Link the mask file to the artwork and drawing revision used for printing. Mark which logo, illustration or other supplied object the gloss follows and which areas it intentionally leaves uncoated.

Show folds, cut edges and glue areas on the same working view. These are location fields for printer/converter confirmation, not an invitation to apply a generic registration tolerance. Keep any technical clearance in the selected supplier’s own proposal.

Attach the coating grade to the zone decision

The ACTEGA grade sheet is an example of a coating whose own technical description identifies glueability and stamping limitations. That demonstrates why the exact grade matters; it does not mean every gloss layer has identical behavior.

Ask the printer and converter to identify the coating grade and any excluded bonding areas on the offered drawing. If the mask crosses a joint, retain that as a question for the people responsible for both coating and gluing. A decorative mask preview cannot settle the joint.

Review a named proof or formed sample with the mask and artwork boundaries visible. Record a shifted edge, incomplete coverage or another located observation alongside the evidence type and conditions. The next response should identify the object and proposed correction.
